Works by Jewish composers or others deemed non-Aryan were banned, including the classical figures Gustav Mahler, Felix Mendelssohn, Arnold Schoenberg, George Gershwin, and Claude Debussy. In a related move, Irving Berlin’s popular songs were banned in their entirety due to his Jewish background, illustrating the regime’s extensive cultural suppression aligned with its ideological aims.

ai_text: The Guild of Music Supervisors Award for Best Song Written and/or Recording Created for a Film is a category within the Guild of Music Supervisors Awards that recognizes songs written and/or recorded specifically for feature films. It is presented annually as part of the awards program, honoring music that was created directly for cinematic releases. The category was introduced at the Guild's sixth annual awards ceremony and has been awarded each year since its inception.

human_text: The 2023–24 Czech Cup, known as the MOL Cup for sponsorship reasons, is the 31st season of the annual knockout football tournament of the Czech Republic. The winners qualify for the third qualifying round of the 2024–25 UEFA Europa League.

human_text: Sobhuza II, the King of Eswatini at the time the war broke out, struck a deal with the British government, agreeing to help gather volunteers for the war effort within the country in exchange for the British allowing for greater Swazi autonomy in the future. A few thousand Swazi men ended up volunteering to fight alongside the Allies. Swazis enlisted into the African Auxiliary Pioneer Corps which went on to serve in Egypt and Libya during the Western Desert campaign, part of the larger North Africa campaign, and also participated in the Allied invasion of Italy. One notable Swazi veteran of the war is Mnikwa Dlamini, who later became the Chief of Hhelehhele.
ai_text: During the early years of World War II, Sobhuza II was the king of Eswatini. He brokered an agreement with the British government whereby Swaziland would contribute volunteers to the Allied war effort in exchange for the prospect of greater autonomy in the future. A few thousand Swazi men volunteered to fight for the Allies, enlisting in the African Auxiliary Pioneer Corps. The corps served in Egypt and Libya as part of the Western Desert campaign in North Africa, and later participated in the Allied invasion of Italy. A notable Swazi veteran was Mnikwa Dlamini, who would later become the Chief of Hhelehhele.

human_text: Eswatini (known at the time as Swaziland) remained a British protectorate throughout World War II. As such, it fought alongside the Allies against the Axis. While no large scale battles or major military operations took place in or around Eswatini, the colony did supply the Allies with troops during the war. World War II was also responsible for several important domestic developments in Eswatini.
ai_text: During World War II, Eswatini—then known as Swaziland—remained a British protectorate and supported the Allies in their fight against the Axis Powers. Although no large-scale battles or major military operations occurred in or near the territory, Swaziland contributed troops to the Allied war effort. The war era also brought several notable domestic developments to Eswatini, reflecting changes within its administration and society under wartime conditions.

human_text: On July 6, 2023, Eilish announced the single on her social media. In an accompanying announcement, she said that the song "means the absolute" world to her. The singer hoped that the track would "change lives" and told her fans to "get ready to sob". A snippet of the single appeared in a trailer for the film on July 10, 2023. Eilish also teased the single and music video on Twitter on July 12. The song was released the following day on July 13. In the film itself, which premiered the same month, the song accompanies a scene in which Barbie meets the spirit of her creator Ruth Handler.
ai_text: What Was I Made For? is a song by American singer Billie Eilish, released on July 13, 2023, as part of the soundtrack for the 2023 film Barbie. Eilish announced the track on July 6, 2023 through social media, describing the song as meaning the world to her and expressing the hope that it would change lives, while urging fans to prepare to sob. A short snippet was shown in a trailer for the film on July 10, 2023. She continued to tease the single and its music video on Twitter on July 12, 2023. In the film, the song accompanies a scene in which Barbie meets the spirit of her creator, Ruth Handler.

human_text: The music video for "What Was I Made For?" was released alongside the single on July 13, 2023. The video, directed by Eilish herself, was shot in one take, and portrays Eilish in a yellow dress (the color Stereotypical Barbie wears at the end of the film) and a blonde wig styled with bangs and a high ponytail similar to the hairstyle of the original 1959 Barbie. Eilish sits at a school desk in an empty, monochromatic space. From a Barbie-themed case, she removes and examines doll clothing resembling outfits Eilish has worn publicly in the past, which she organizes on a miniature hanging rack. As the song progresses, a brief earthquake, a strong wind, and rain threaten to disrupt her efforts. When the rain ends, Eilish quickly stuffs the doll clothes back into their case and walks away, taking the doll case with her. Shortly after the song's ending, Eilish returns briefly to collect a forgotten accessory before exiting once more.
ai_text: The music video for What Was I Made For? was released on July 13, 2023, alongside the single, and was directed by Billie Eilish herself, with the footage filmed in a single continuous take. A Barbie-themed case containing miniature doll clothing that mirrors outfits Eilish has worn publicly serves as the central prop. In the sequence, she removes and examines the doll garments, organizing them on a miniature hanging rack while facing interruptions from a brief earthquake, strong wind, and rain that threaten progress. After the rain subsides, she stuffs the clothes back into the case and leaves with the case in hand, and she briefly returns after the song’s ending to collect a forgotten accessory before exiting again.

human_text: Longkou West Station (simplified Chinese: 龙口西站; traditional Chinese: 龍口西站; pinyin: Lóngkǒuxī Zhàn; Cantonese Yale: Lǔngháusāi Jaahm) is a station of Line 11 of the Guangzhou Metro. human_text: At the beginning of the planning of Line 11, the station was named Longkou East, and later began construction under the name of Tianhe East. On 20 September 2024, the station completed the "three rights" transfer.
ai_text: Longkou West station is a station on Line 11 that underwent several name changes during its development: during the planning stage it was designated Longkou East, and during construction it was renamed Tianhe East. human_text: Vox Media, Inc. is an American mass media company founded in Washington, D.C. with operational headquarters in Lower Manhattan, New York City. The company was established in November 2011 by CEO Jim Bankoff and Trei Brundrett to encompass SB Nation (a sports blog network founded in 2003 by Tyler Bleszinski, Markos Moulitsas, and Jerome Armstrong) and The Verge (a technology news website launched alongside Vox Media). Bankoff had been the CEO for SB Nation since 2009.
ai_text: Vox Media, Inc. is an American mass media company founded in November 2011 in Washington, D.C., by Jim Bankoff and Trei Brundrett. It is headquartered in Lower Manhattan, New York City. The company was created to oversee SB Nation, a sports blog network established in 2003 by Tyler Bleszinski, Markos Moulitsas, and Jerome Armstrong, and The Verge, a technology news website that launched concurrently with Vox Media. Bankoff had served as chief executive of SB Nation since 2009 prior to Vox Media's founding.

human_text: In February 2018, it was reported that Vox Media would be laying off around 50 employees, particularly surrounding video production. CEO Jim Bankoff stated previously that the company planned to exit native video for Facebook due to "unreliable monetization and promotion". The memo announcing the layoffs argued that despite its success, native video "won't be viable audience or revenue growth drivers for us relative to other investments we are making", and that the company wanted to focus more on podcasting and Vox Entertainment. The layoffs represented around 5% of Vox's workforce.
ai_text: In February 2018, Vox Media laid off approximately 50 employees, predominantly from its video production teams, a reduction that comprised about 5% of its workforce. The move followed CEO Jim Bankoff’s prior indication that Vox planned to exit native video on Facebook due to inconsistent monetization and limited promotional reach. An internal layoff memo stated that, despite its success, native video would not constitute a viable driver of audience growth or revenue compared with other investments. As a result, Vox redirected its strategy to place greater emphasis on podcasting and Vox Entertainment.

human_text: As of June 2012, the U.S. Navy had four minesweepers deployed to the Persian Gulf to address regional instabilities. The Royal Navy also has four minesweepers stationed in the Persian Gulf as part of the 9th Mine Counter-Measures Squadron.

human_text: Minesweeping made significant advancements during World War II.  Combatant nations quickly adapted ships to the task of minesweeping, including Australia's 35 civilian ships that became auxiliary minesweepers.  Both Allied and Axis countries made heavy use of minesweepers throughout the war.  Historian Gordon Williamson wrote that "Germany's minesweepers alone formed a massive proportion of its total strength, and are very much the unsung heroes of the Kriegsmarine."  Naval mines remained a threat even after the war ended, and minesweeping crews were still active after VJ Day.
ai_text: During World War II, significant advances in minesweeping emerged as nations reoriented and repurposed vessels for mine clearance duties. Several states adapted ships for minesweeping, with Australia converting 35 civilian vessels into auxiliary minesweepers to bolster coastal and convoy protection. Both the Allied and Axis powers relied heavily on minesweeping operations throughout the conflict, reflecting the central role of naval mines in wartime strategy. In the Kriegsmarine, minesweepers formed a substantial portion of overall strength and are regarded as an essential, though often overlooked, component of German maritime power. The threat posed by naval mines did not end with hostilities, as minesweeping crews remained active after VJ Day to clear contested waters and safeguard postwar navigation.

human_text: At the onset of the battle, KMT-CPC relations were at a low point following the still recent New Fourth Army incident in early 1941. As a result, the nearby 8th Route Army refused to assist the surrounded Nationalists. South Shanxi was later remembered in China as one of the worst defeats of the entire war.
ai_text: Set during the Second Sino-Japanese War, the Battle of South Shanxi unfolded amid deteriorating Kuomintang–Communist relations after the New Fourth Army incident in early 1941. In the surrounding area, the Eighth Route Army declined to come to the aid of the encircled Nationalist forces, effectively leaving them to fight without Communist support. The engagement concluded in a heavy Nationalist defeat, an outcome that is remembered in China as one of the war's worst defeats.

human_text: Discovery Primea is a 68-storey mixed-use residential tower and one of the tallest buildings in the Philippines located in Makati along Ayala Avenue. It stands on the former Gilarmi Apartments, then co-owned by the first ever crowned Miss Universe Armi Kuusela and ex-husband businessman Virgilio Hilario, and one of the earliest urban residential condominiums in the Makati Central Business District. JTKC, Inc. is the developer of the residential condominium and one of earliest developer of residential condominium units in the Philippines. The latter also owns the Discovery Suites, a service-apartment in the Ortigas Center business district in Mandaluyong. The residential tower was opened in February 2015.

human_text: Operation Musketeer I, II, III (1944-1945)   – American and Filipino campaign to defeat and expel the Imperial Japanese forces occupying the Philippines.
ai_text: Operation Musketeer I, II, and III, conducted from 1944 to 1945, were a series of World War II operations carried out by United States and Filipino forces with the objective of defeating and expelling the Imperial Japanese forces occupying the Philippines.

page_title: List of World War II military operations
human_text: Margarethe (1944)  – German occupation of Hungary.  Döme Sztójay, an avid supporter of the Nazis, became the new Hungarian Prime Minister with the aid of a Nazi military governor.
ai_text: In 1944, the German operation Margarethe led to the occupation of Hungary during World War II. Döme Sztójay, a pro-Nazi figure, was subsequently appointed Hungary’s prime minister, with his installation aided by a German military governor who operated within the occupation authorities.

human_text: The Porter-class destroyers were a class of eight 1,850-ton large destroyers in the United States Navy. Like the preceding Farragut-class, their construction was authorized by Congress on 26 April 1916, but funding was delayed considerably. They were designed based on a 1,850-ton standard displacement limit imposed by the London Naval Treaty; the treaty's tonnage limit allowed 13 ships of this size, and the similar Somers class was built later to meet the limit. The first four Porters were laid down in 1933 by New York Shipbuilding in Camden, New Jersey, and the next four in 1934 at Bethlehem Steel Corporation in Quincy, Massachusetts. All were commissioned in 1936 except Winslow, which was commissioned in 1937. They were built in response to the large Fubuki-class destroyers that the Imperial Japanese Navy was building at the time and were initially designated as flotilla leaders. They served extensively in World War II, in the Pacific War, the Atlantic, and in the Americas. Porter was the class' only loss, in the Battle of the Santa Cruz Islands on 26 October 1942.
ai_text: The Porter-class destroyers comprised eight large ships of about 1,850 tons standard displacement in the United States Navy. Construction was authorized by Congress on 26 April 1916, but funding was delayed. The design conformed to the London Naval Treaty’s 1,850-ton limit, which allowed thirteen ships of this size, with a later Somers class built to satisfy the limit. The first four vessels were laid down in 1933 by New York Shipbuilding in Camden, New Jersey, and the remaining four in 1934 by Bethlehem Steel in Quincy, Massachusetts. All boats were commissioned in 1936 except Winslow, which entered service in 1937. The class was developed in response to Japan’s large Fubuki-class destroyers and was initially designated to serve as flotilla leaders. During World War II, Porter-class ships saw extensive service across the Pacific, the Atlantic, and the Americas. Porter was the sole loss of the class, sunk at the Battle of the Santa Cruz Islands on 26 October 1942.

human_text: McDougal, Winslow, and Moffett were among the five destroyers and two cruisers  that supported the Roosevelt-Churchill conference at Placentia Bay near Argentia, Newfoundland that resulted in the Atlantic Charter in August 1941. Selfridge and Phelps were in port during the attack on Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941 and engaged enemy aircraft. The class served in the Battle of the Atlantic, in the Pacific War, and escorted convoys in the Americas. Phelps was at the Battle of the Coral Sea and the Battle of Midway, scuttling the disabled aircraft carrier Lexington with torpedoes at the former battle and picking up some of the crew from the sea following the orderly ship abandonment. Balch rescued survivors of the aircraft carrier Yorktown at Midway. While operating out of Trinidad in the Caribbean, Moffett assisted in sinking two U-boats, U-128 and U-604. Notable engagements for other ships of the class included the invasion of Guadalcanal and the Marianas campaign. By September 1944 the class was concentrated in the Atlantic. Porter was the class's only loss, in the Battle of the Santa Cruz Islands on 26 October 1942. Selfridge lost her bow to a torpedo in the Naval Battle of Vella Lavella on 6 October 1943, but was repaired. McDougal and Winslow were reclassified as AG-126 and AG-127 in September 1945 and modified for anti-kamikaze research in a similar configuration to Gearing-class radar picket destroyers. All except Winslow were scrapped shortly after the war; Winslow remained in service as a training ship until 1950 and was scrapped in 1959. Winslow was the longest serving by far of all destroyers commissioned in the 1930s and the last by far to go to the ship breakers.
ai_text: Porter-class destroyers consisted of seven vessels: Porter, McDougal, Winslow, Moffett, Selfridge, Phelps, and Balch. In August 1941, three of them—McDougal, Winslow, and Moffett—took part in the escort group that supported the Atlantic Charter conference at Placentia Bay alongside five destroyers and two cruisers. Selfridge and Phelps were in port during the attack on Pearl Harbor and engaged incoming aircraft. The class operated in both major theaters of World War II, seeing action in the Battle of the Atlantic and the Pacific War while also escorting convoys in the Americas. Phelps fought at the Coral Sea and Midway, where she scuttled the disabled aircraft carrier Lexington and helped rescue its crew. Balch assisted in Midway by rescuing Yorktown survivors. Moffett contributed to the destruction of two U-boats, U-128 and U-604, while stationed near Trinidad in the Caribbean. Other ships of the class also took part in the Guadalcanal invasion and the Marianas campaign. By September 1944, the class had become concentrated in the Atlantic theater. Porter suffered the class’s sole loss, at the Battle of the Santa Cruz Islands on 26 October 1942. Selfridge lost her bow to a torpedo at the Naval Battle of Vella Lavella on 6 October 1943, but was subsequently repaired. In September 1945 McDougal and Winslow were redesignated AG-126 and AG-127 and modified for anti-kamikaze research, in a configuration akin to Gearing-class radar-picket destroyers. With the end of the war, all ships except Winslow were scrapped; Winslow, used as a training vessel, remained in service until 1950 and was scrapped in 1959, making it the most enduring destroyer commissioned in the 1930s and the last of the class to be scrapped.

human_text: On 22 June 1941, the Axis invaded the Soviet Union. Three days later, the Soviet Union conducted an air raid on Finnish cities which prompted Finland to declare war and allow German troops in Finland to begin offensive warfare. By September 1941, Finland had regained its post–Winter War concessions to the Soviet Union in Karelia. The Finnish Army continued its offensive past the 1939 border during the invasion of East Karelia and halted it only around 30–32 km (19–20 mi) from the centre of Leningrad. It participated in besieging the city by cutting the northern supply routes and by digging in until 1944. In Lapland, joint German–Finnish forces failed to capture Murmansk or cut the Kirov (Murmansk) Railway. The Soviet Vyborg–Petrozavodsk offensive in June and August 1944 drove the Finns from most of the territories that they had gained during the war, but the Finnish Army halted the offensive in August 1944.
ai_text: The Continuation War was a conflict between Finland and the Soviet Union that ran from 1941 to 1944, in alignment with Germany’s campaign against the Soviet Union. On June 25, 1941, a Soviet air raid on Finnish cities prompted Finland to declare war and to permit German troops to operate within Finnish territory. By September 1941 Finland had regained post‑Winter War concessions in Karelia. The Finnish Army advanced beyond the 1939 border into East Karelia, reaching about 30–32 kilometers from the center of Leningrad and taking part in the siege by cutting northern supply routes and holding positions until 1944. In Lapland, German–Finnish forces failed to capture Murmansk or to sever the Kirov Railway. In 1944, the Soviet Vyborg–Petrozavodsk offensive in June and August drove Finns from much of the territories they had gained, but the Finnish Army halted the offensive in August 1944.

human_text: The number of Soviet prisoners of war in Finland was estimated by Finnish historians to be around 64,000, 56,000 of whom were captured in 1941. Around 2,600 to 2,800 Soviet prisoners of war were rendered to Germany in exchange for roughly 2,200 Finnish prisoners of war. Of the Soviet prisoners, at least 18,318 were documented to have died in Finnish prisoner of war camps. Finnish archival sources indicate that the highest mortality rates were observed in the largest prisoner of war camps, with mortality rates as high as 41%. For small camps, the comparable mortality rate was under 5%. Nearly 85% of the deaths happened between November 1941 and September 1942 with the highest monthly number of deaths, 2,665, recorded in February 1942. For comparison, the amount of deaths in February 1943 was 92. Historian Oula Silvennoinen attributes the amount of Soviet deaths to several factors, which include Finnish unpreparedness to handle unexpectedly large amounts of prisoners resulting in overcrowding, a lack of warm clothing among prisoners captured predominantly during the summer offensive, limited supplies of food (often made worse by camp personnel stealing food for themselves), and disease as a result of the previous factors. According to historian Antti Kujala, approximately 1,200 prisoners were shot, "most" of whom illegally.
ai_text: During the Continuation War, Finland held a substantial number of Soviet prisoners of war, with estimates placing the total at around 64,000 and about 56,000 captured in 1941. A subset of these, between 2,600 and 2,800, were transferred to Germany in exchange for roughly 2,200 Finnish POWs. In Finnish captivity, at least 18,318 Soviet POWs died. Mortality was highest in the largest camps, approaching 41 percent, while smaller camps recorded rates of under 5 percent. Approximately 85 percent of deaths occurred between November 1941 and September 1942, and peak monthly fatalities reached 2,665 in February 1942, with 92 deaths in February 1943. Scholars such as Oula Silvennoinen attribute the deaths to overcrowding, inadequate preparation, insufficient warm clothing, and limited food—often diverted by camp staff—and to disease. Antti Kujala states that around 1,200 prisoners were shot, most of them illegally.

human_text: In 2013, Jeffrey Goldberg reported that, in Obama's view, "with each new settlement announcement, Netanyahu is moving his country down a path toward near-total isolation." He said both movements seek to bring justice and equal rights to historically persecuted peoples, explaining: "To me, being pro-Israel and pro-Jewish is part and parcel with the values that I've been fighting for since I was politically conscious and started getting involved in politics." Obama expressed support for Israel's right to defend itself during the 2014 Israel–Gaza conflict. In 2015, Obama was harshly criticized by Israel for advocating and signing the Iran Nuclear Deal; Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who had advocated the U.S. congress to oppose it, said the deal was "dangerous" and "bad."
ai_text: From 2013 through 2015, Barack Obama articulated a nuanced stance on Israel and its security, balancing advocacy for regional stability with support for Israel’s right to defend itself. In 2013, journalist Jeffrey Goldberg reported that Obama believed each new settlement announcement pushed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government toward broad international isolation. In 2014, he drew a parallel between the Zionist movement and the U.S. civil rights movement, arguing that both pursue justice and equal rights for historically persecuted peoples, and he reiterated that being pro-Israel and pro-Jewish was part of the political values he had long fought for. During the 2014 Israel–Gaza conflict, Obama affirmed Israel’s right to defend itself. The following year, he faced sharp criticism from Israel after advocating for and signing the Iran nuclear deal. Netanyahu opposed the agreement, urging the U.S. Congress to reject it and labeling it dangerous and bad.

human_text: In 2011, Obama ordered a drone strike in Yemen which targeted and killed Anwar al-Awlaki, an American imam suspected of being a leading Al-Qaeda organizer. al-Awlaki became the first U.S. citizen to be targeted and killed by a U.S. drone strike. The Department of Justice released a memo justifying al-Awlaki's death as a lawful act of war, while civil liberties advocates described it as a violation of al-Awlaki's constitutional right to due process. The killing led to significant controversy. His teenage son and young daughter, also Americans, were later killed in separate U.S. military actions, although they were not targeted specifically.
ai_text: During his presidency, Barack Obama authorized a 2011 drone strike in Yemen aimed at Anwar al-Awlaki, an American imam believed to have been a senior figure within Al-Qaeda. Al-Awlaki thus became the first U.S. citizen to be targeted and killed by a U.S. drone strike. The Department of Justice released a memo asserting that the operation was a lawful act of war under the authorization for use of military force, a stance that civil liberties advocates characterized as a violation of due process and that provoked substantial controversy. In the aftermath, al-Awlaki's teenage son and younger daughter, both American citizens, were killed in separate U.S. military actions, though not targeted directly.

human_text: On December 20, 1944, Eisenhower was appointed to the rank of General of the Army, placing him in the company of George Marshall, Henry "Hap" Arnold, and Douglas MacArthur, the only four men to achieve the rank in World War II. Along with Omar Bradley, they were the only five men to achieve the rank since the August 5, 1888, death of Philip Sheridan, and the only five men to hold the rank of five-star general. The rank was created by an Act of Congress on a temporary basis, when Public Law 78-482 was passed on December 14, 1944, as a temporary rank, subject to reversion to permanent rank six months after the end of the war. The temporary rank was declared permanent on March 23, 1946, by Public Law 333 of the 79th Congress, which also awarded full pay and allowances in the grade to those on the retired list. It was created to give the most senior American commanders parity of rank with their British counterparts holding the ranks of field marshal and admiral of the fleet.

human_text: From 1952 to 1989, 2001 to 2014, 2020 and 2024, the "Miss Universe" title and the "First", "Second," "Third," and "Fourth Runner-Up" titles were awarded among the last five remaining finalists (Top 5) in the pageant. human_text: The island of Taiwan lies across the Tropic of Cancer, and its climate is influenced by the East Asian Monsoon. Northern Taiwan has a humid subtropical climate, with substantial seasonal variation of temperatures, while parts of central and most of southern Taiwan have a tropical monsoon climate where seasonal temperature variations are less noticeable, with temperatures typically varying from warm to hot. During the winter (November to March), the northeast experiences steady rain, while the central and southern parts of the island are mostly sunny.  The summer monsoon (from May to October) accounts for 90% of the annual precipitation in the south, but only 60% in the north. The average rainfall is approximately 2,600 mm per year.

The smaller destroyer leaders were reclassified as destroyers and the larger as cruisers by the United States Navy 1975 ship reclassification so destroyer escorts could be reclassified as frigates (FF) in conformance with international usage of the term.

human_text: The Right to Financial Privacy Act of 1978 (RFPA; codified at 12 U.S.C. ch. 35, § 3401 et seq.) is a United States federal law, Title XI of the Financial Institutions Regulatory and Interest Rate Control Act of 1978, that gives the customers of financial institutions the right to some level of privacy from government searches.
ai_text: The Right to Financial Privacy Act of 1978 (RFPA) is a United States federal law enacted as Title XI of the Financial Institutions Regulatory and Interest Rate Control Act of 1978. It is codified at 12 U.S.C. chapter 35, beginning with section 3401, and establishes protections for the privacy of customers’ financial records by governing the manner and extent to which government authorities may access those records, thereby granting individuals a measure of privacy from government searches.

human_text: Under the RFPA, the FBI could obtain records with a national security letter (NSL) only if the FBI could first demonstrate the person was a foreign power or an agent of a foreign power. Compliance by the recipient of the NSL was voluntary, and states' consumer privacy laws often allowed financial institutions to decline the requests. In 1986, Congress amended RFPA to allow the government to compel disclosure of the requested information. The USA PATRIOT Act of 2001 amended the RFPA.
ai_text: The Right to Financial Privacy Act (RFPA) governs access to individuals' financial records held by financial institutions. Compliance with such letters was voluntary, and many states' privacy laws permitted financial institutions to decline the requests. In 1986, Congress amended the RFPA to authorize the government to compel disclosure of the requested information. The act was later amended by the USA PATRIOT Act of 2001.

human_text: Ships are increasingly being scuttled as a method of disposal. The economic benefit of scuttling a ship includes removal of ongoing operational expense to keep the vessel seaworthy. Controversy surrounds the practice. The USS Oriskany was scuttled with 700 pounds of PCBs remaining on board as a component in cable insulation,  contravening the Stockholm Convention on safe disposal of persistent organic pollutants, which has zero tolerance for PCB dumping in marine environments. The planned scuttling of the Australian frigate HMAS Adelaide at Avoca Beach, New South Wales in March 2010 was placed on hold after resident action groups aired concerns about possible impact on the area's tides and that the removal of dangerous substances from the ship was not thorough enough. Further cleanup work on the hulk was ordered, and despite further attempts to delay, Adelaide was scuttled on 13 April 2011.

human_text: During World War II, German Type XXI submarines (also known as "Elektroboote") were the first submarines designed to operate submerged for extended periods. Initially they were to carry hydrogen peroxide for long-term, fast air-independent propulsion, but were ultimately built with very large batteries instead. At the end of the War, the British and Soviets experimented with hydrogen peroxide/kerosene (paraffin) engines that could run surfaced and submerged. The results were not encouraging. Though the Soviet Union deployed a class of submarines with this engine type (codenamed Quebec by NATO), they were considered unsuccessful.

Although initial plans envisioned hydrogen peroxide as a means of long-term air-independent propulsion, the vessels were ultimately built with very large batteries to power electric motors while submerged. As World War II ended, both the British and the Soviets tested hydrogen peroxide/kerosene propulsion systems that could operate in both surfaced and submerged conditions, but the results of these experiments were not encouraging. The Soviet Union later deployed a class of submarines using this propulsion method (NATO reporting name Quebec), a design that did not prove successful.

human_text: All surface ships, as well as surfaced submarines, are in a positively buoyant condition, weighing less than the volume of water they would displace if fully submerged. To submerge hydrostatically, a ship must have negative buoyancy, either by increasing its own weight or decreasing its displacement of water. To control their displacement and weight, submarines have ballast tanks, which can hold varying amounts of water and air.
ai_text: At the surface, surface ships and submarines that are not fully submerged exhibit positive buoyancy, meaning their total weight is less than the weight of the water they would displace if completely submerged. To submerge, a submarine must become negatively buoyant, which is achieved either by increasing its overall weight or by decreasing the amount of water it displaces. The principal means of doing so is a ballast system consisting of ballast tanks that can hold varying amounts of water and air; filling ballast tanks with water raises the vehicle’s weight and lowers its buoyancy to permit descent, while expelling water and introducing air reduces weight and increases buoyancy for ascent. In this way, ballast tanks provide precise control over both displacement and weight, enabling depth changes and station-keeping.

human_text: ISSN does not offer resolution mechanisms like a digital object identifier (DOI) or a URN does, so the DOI is used as a URN for articles, with (for historical reasons) no need for an ISSN's existence.
ai_text: ISSN, which serves as a unique identifier for serial publications, does not provide a mechanism to resolve a given identifier into a location or resource on the web. In contrast, DOIs offer resolvable links to digital content and can function as a Uniform Resource Name for individual articles. Consequently, DOIs are commonly used as the URN for scholarly articles within many publishing and indexing workflows. Historically, the utility of ISSNs in this specific capacity has been regarded as largely unnecessary, reflecting a shift toward DOI-based-resolution systems for article identification.

human_text: In domestic affairs, Nixon advocated a policy of "New Federalism", in which federal powers and responsibilities would be shifted to state governments. However, he faced a Democratic Congress that did not share his goals and, in some cases, enacted legislation over his veto. Nixon's proposed reform of federal welfare programs did not pass Congress, but Congress did adopt one aspect of his proposal in the form of Supplemental Security Income, which provides aid to low-income individuals who are aged or disabled. The Nixon administration adopted a "low profile" on school desegregation, but the administration enforced court desegregation orders and implemented the first affirmative action plan in the United States. Nixon also presided over the creation of the Environmental Protection Agency and the passage of major environmental laws like the Clean Water Act, although that law was vetoed by Nixon and passed by override. Economically, the Nixon years saw the start of a period of "stagflation" that would continue into the 1970s.

Economically, the period initiated the stagflation trend—a combination of inflation and slow growth—that would persist into the 1970s.

human_text: The development of the "oiler" paralleled the change from coal- to oil-fired boilers in warships. Prior to the adoption of oil fired machinery, navies could extend the range of their ships either by maintaining coaling stations or for warships to raft together with colliers and for coal to be manhandled aboard. Though arguments related to fuel security were made against such a change, the ease with which liquid fuel could be transferred led in part to its adoption by navies worldwide.One of the first generation of "blue-water" navy oiler support vessels was the British RFA Kharki, active 1911 in the run-up to the First World War. Such vessels heralded the transition from coal to oil as the fuel of warships and removed the need to rely on, and operate within range of coaling stations. During the Second World War, the United States Navy's dramatically enlarged fleets, especially those in the Pacific Theater, required massive quantities of black oil, diesel oil, avgas, and other fuels and lubricants to support American land, sea, and air operations against remote, widely dispersed Japanese forces. Those supply demands resulted in U.S. Navy personnel refining many established practices for oilers and creating new procedures for replenishing warships while underway and for transporting highly combustible materials with increased effectiveness through hostile waters and over vast ocean distances.

Although fuel-security concerns were voiced, the relative ease of transferring liquid fuel facilitated the global adoption of replenishment oilers. An early long-range example was the British Royal Fleet Auxiliary vessel Kharki, which operated in 1911, before World War I. Consequently, oilers signaled the shift from coal to oil and reduced dependence on fixed coaling infrastructure. In World War II, the United States Navy's expansion in the Pacific required vast quantities of fuel oils, diesel, aviation gasoline, and related lubricants, prompting refinements in oiler operations and the development of underway replenishment procedures to move highly combustible liquids through hostile waters and over great distances.

human_text: A declaration of war is a formal act by which one nation goes to war against another. The declaration is usually the act of delivering a performative speech or the presentation of a signed document by an authorized party of a national government in order to create a state of war between two or more sovereign states. The official international protocol for declaring war was defined in The Hague Peace Conference of 1907 (or Hague II). For the diplomatic maneuvering behind these events, which led to hostilities between nations during World War II, see Diplomatic history of World War II.

These declarations are typically conveyed through a public proclamation or a signed instrument issued by an authorized government representative, and they create a state of war between the involved sovereign states. The international protocol governing such declarations was established at the Hague Peace Conference of 1907 (Hague II). The diplomatic maneuvering surrounding these events in the lead-up to and during World War II is discussed in the broader context of the Diplomatic history of World War II.

human_text: The next major feature added to the standard was Multiview Video Coding (MVC). Specified in Annex H of H.264/AVC, MVC enables the construction of bitstreams that represent more than one view of a video scene. Two profiles were developed in the MVC work: Multiview High profile supports an arbitrary number of views, and Stereo High profile is designed specifically for two-view stereoscopic video. Then small scale trials of what would go on to become the large scale, death camp gas chambers were designed and carried out. These trials showed the authorities that this method facilitated the means to murder the largest number of prisoners without "excessive" initial panic. The character 草 appears in this sense, for example, in 草稿 (Modern Mandarin cǎogǎo, "rough draft") and 草擬 (cǎonǐ, "to draft [a document or plan]"). human_text: Cursive script forms of Chinese characters are also the origin of the Japanese hiragana script. In Japan, the sōgana cursive script was considered to be suitable for women's writing, and thus came to be referred to as women’s script (女手, onnade).  Onnade was later applied to hiragana as well. In contrast, kanji was referred to as men’s script (男手, otokode).

By contrast, the remaining logographic characters were called kanji and were described as the men’s script (otoko-de).

In a representative configuration with a pulse repetition frequency of 2 kHz and a transmit frequency of 1 GHz, the highest unambiguous radial velocity that can be reliably retrieved is about 150 m/s (roughly 340 mph). This limit follows from the Nyquist criterion, given the radar wavelength λ ≈ c/f ≈ 0.3 meters, which yields a maximum unambiguous velocity v_max = (λ·PRF)/4 ≈ 150 m/s. As a result, objects moving faster than this—such as an aircraft traveling at 1,000 m/s (approximately 2,200 mph)—would exceed the unambiguous Doppler range, rendering their radial velocity measurements unreliable without adjustments such as increasing the PRF or employing additional observing strategies.

human_text: Sean-nós, or "old style" dance is a form of Irish dancing which originated from western regions of Ireland. It has been described variously as a regional style of stepdancing, and as an entirely separate style that was virtually unknown outside small areas until the late 20th century. It is distinguished by footwork which is percussive but low to the ground in comparison to step dancing, and by its more freeform nature. Performers use a more relaxed posture, and improvise steps to fit with music. Typically, sean-nós dances are performed in small spaces, traditionally doors laid flat and table tops.

It is characterized by percussion-heavy, low-to-the-ground footwork and a freer, more improvisational approach to movement. Performers typically maintain a relaxed posture and invent steps to match the music as they perform. Performances are commonly held in very confined spaces, historically with doors laid flat on the floor and makeshift surfaces such as tabletops serving as stages.

human_text: Speed is sometimes incorrectly expressed as "knots per hour", which would mean "nautical miles per hour per hour" and thus would refer to acceleration.
ai_text: Knot is a unit of speed used primarily in maritime and aviation contexts, defined as one nautical mile traversed in one hour. Describing velocity in a form that includes an additional per-hour component would be incorrect, since it would amount to nautical miles per hour per hour, effectively an acceleration term rather than speed. Therefore, speed is ordinarily expressed simply in knots, not in a per-hour form.

human_text: The indicated airspeed is close to the true airspeed only at sea level in standard conditions and at low speeds. At 11000 m (36000 ft), an indicated airspeed of 300 kn may correspond to a true airspeed of 500 kn in standard conditions.
ai_text: Knots are the unit in which indicated airspeed (IAS) and true airspeed (TAS) are expressed in aviation, but the relationship between the two speeds varies with altitude and atmospheric conditions. IAS closely approximates TAS only at sea level under standard atmospheric conditions and at low speeds. At higher altitudes, such as 11,000 meters (36,000 feet), an IAS of 300 kn may correspond to a TAS of about 500 kn under standard conditions.

human_text: During her years of service, Discoverer's assigned projects varied from cruise to cruise, and it also was common for several different projects to be carried out aboard her simultaneously. Discoverer's major projects included the Aerosol Characterization Experiment (ACE), the Radiatively Important Trace Species (RITS), the World Ocean Circulation Experiment (WOCE), the  Combined Sensor Project (CSP), the Global Ocean-Atmosphere-Land System (GOALS) project, and NOAA's Vents project (involving the study of underwater volcanic and venting activity within 100 nautical miles (190 km) of the coast of the state of Washington along the southern Juan de Fuca Ridge the Blanco fracture zone, and a marginal subduction zone). Ancillary projects, carried out in addition to the main objectives of each cruise, included the Automated Shipboard Aerological Program (ASAP), the Cadet Training Program (for students from the California Maritime Academy, the United States Military Academy, and the United States Naval Academy), marine mammal observations (she averaged 23 sightings of marine mammals per year), use of her Shipboard Environmental Data Acquisition System (SEAS) (averaging 1,700 weather reports per year, she was among the top ten reporting ships in the program in each year from 1989 through 1996 and was the top reporter in 1992, 1993, and 1994), and the Teacher at Sea Program (in which teachers came aboard to observe operations in the Vents program).

human_text: During 1987, the United States Navy used Discoverer as a replacement for the Military Sealift Command oceanographic survey ship USNS Bowditch, installing Bowditch's narrow-beam mapping sonars, doppler sonar, and navigational equipment aboard Discoverer.

human_text: The Indigenous people were not consulted in the Treaty of Oregon, which saw the United States and Great Britain define and recognize each other's claims to the area. This overstepping of jurisdiction inevitably led to conflict as Great Britain was incapable of exercising the control they claimed over the river valley. As a wave of immigrants flooded into the Fraser River Valley because of the Fraser Canyon Gold Rush, the British were unable to maintain order without the cooperation of the local indigenous peoples, and the Fraser Canyon War broke out. The war was resolved with a series of treaties, none of which remain to this day, but which evidently included the regulation of immigration and the continuation of mining on the river by the indigenous inhabitants and the new immigrants. This war was part of a series of local conflicts surrounding the arrival of settlers ahead of American and British capacity to maintain order and refusal to cooperate with or recognize indigenous land claims and demands. These conflicts were pivotal in many aspects to the settlement of the West Coast in both Canada and the United States.
ai_text: Fraser Valley, along the lower Fraser River, experienced early sovereignty disputes when the Treaty of Oregon delineated U.S. and British claims to the river valley, yet Indigenous peoples were not consulted in its negotiation. The treaty overstepped jurisdiction, limiting Britain's ability to enforce its asserted authority over the valley's lands and waters. The prospect of settlement attracted immigrants during the Fraser Canyon Gold Rush, a development that intensified tensions and challenged British efforts to maintain order without the cooperation of local Indigenous communities. The ensuing Fraser Canyon War ended with a series of treaties that regulated immigration and allowed continued mining by both Indigenous inhabitants and new arrivals; none of these agreements remains in force today. These conflicts were part of broader clashes over land rights and settler arrival that helped shape the pattern of settlement on Canada’s West Coast and the adjacent United States.

It is divided into the Upper Fraser Valley and Lower Fraser Valley by the Vedder River mouth at the eastern foothills of Sumas Mountain, although the Lower Valley section upstream of McMillan Island and the Salmon River mouth (at Fort Langley) used to be called the Central Fraser Valley up until 1995 (see Central Fraser Valley Regional District).

Some demonyms are borrowed from other languages and function as nicknames or descriptive adjectives for a group. An illustration is Québécois and Québécoise, the feminine form, which in English are used for natives of Quebec, whether the province or the city; alternative forms such as Quebecer or Quebecker are also used.

human_text: Since they are referring to territorially defined groups of people, demonyms are semantically different from ethnonyms (names of ethnic groups). In the English language, there are many polysemic words that have several meanings (including demonymic and ethnonymic uses), and therefore a particular use of any such word depends on the context. For example, the word Thai may be used as a demonym, designating any inhabitant of Thailand, while the same word may also be used as an ethnonym, designating members of the Thai people. Conversely, some groups of people may be associated with multiple demonyms. For example, a native of the United Kingdom may be called a British person, a Briton or, informally, a Brit.

human_text: Social democratic movements in Europe have been of great interest to the CCP since the early 1980s. With the exception of a short period in which the CCP forged party-to-party relations with far-right parties during the 1970s in an effort to halt "Soviet expansionism", the CCP's relations with European social democratic parties were its first serious efforts to establish cordial party-to-party relations with non-communist parties. The CCP credits the European social democrats with creating a "capitalism with a human face". Before the 1980s, the CCP had a highly negative and dismissive view of social democracy, a view dating back to the Second International and the Marxist–Leninist view on the social democratic movement. By the 1980s, that view had changed and the CCP concluded that it could actually learn something from the social democratic movement. CCP delegates were sent all over Europe to observe. By the 1980s, most European social democratic parties were facing electoral decline and in a period of self-reform. The CCP followed this with great interest, laying most weight on reform efforts within the British Labour Party and the Social Democratic Party of Germany. The CCP concluded that both parties were re-elected because they modernized, replacing traditional state socialist tenets with new ones supporting privatization, shedding the belief in big government, conceiving a new view of the welfare state, changing their negative views of the market and moving from their traditional support base of trade unions to entrepreneurs, the young and students.

human_text: At 7:15 am on October 3, 1962, Schirra lifted off aboard his Mercury flight, named Sigma 7. After a minor trajectory deviation early in flight, Sigma 7 achieved orbit. Schirra reported rising suit temperatures, reaching a high of 32 °C (90 °F), before he was able to adjust his suit's cooling system manually. After six orbits, Schirra manually aligned his spacecraft over Africa and performed retrofire. Sigma 7 landed 5 miles (8.0 km) from the recovery ship, the aircraft carrier USS Kearsarge, in the central Pacific Ocean. Once Sigma 7 was on deck, Schirra activated the explosive hatch to egress the spacecraft, and received a large bruise, proving that Grissom had not intentionally opened his hatch on Liberty Bell 7. ai_text: Velocity made good (VMG) is a measure of a sailing vessel’s progress toward a specified mark, combining the boat’s speed with the direction of travel toward the target. Sailing too close to the wind upwind reduces progress because the vessel slows substantially, whereas sailing further downwind increases speed but moves the boat away from the mark to an extent that the speed gain does not meaningfully improve advance toward the target. In practice, VMG reflects the trade-off between speed and angle to the mark, guiding sailors in choosing a balance that maximizes effective progress.

human_text: Because the relationships between the members of the family tree are uncertain, it is difficult to identify the features inherited from the last common ancestor of all molluscs. For example, it is uncertain whether the ancestral mollusc was metameric (composed of repeating units)—if it was, that would suggest an origin from an annelid-like worm. Scientists disagree about this: Giribet and colleagues concluded, in 2006, the repetition of gills and of the foot's retractor muscles were later developments, while in 2007, Sigwart concluded the ancestral mollusc was metameric, and it had a foot used for creeping and a "shell" that was mineralized. In one particular branch of the family tree, the shell of conchiferans is thought to have evolved from the spicules (small spines) of aplacophorans; but this is difficult to reconcile with the embryological origins of spicules.

If the earliest molluscs were metameric, an annelid‑like origin has been suggested as a possibility. In contrast, Giribet et al. (2006) concluded that features such as repeated gills and retractor muscles of the foot are derived characteristics rather than ancestral traits. Additionally, in certain lineages, the evolution of conchiferan shells has been proposed to derive from spicules of aplacophorans, though this scenario is difficult to reconcile with the embryological origin of spicules.

The administration’s response was widely perceived as callous, fueling the anti-war movement. Nevertheless, the United States continued bombing Cambodia as part of Operation Freedom Deal.

human_text: Early opposition drew its inspiration from the Geneva Conference. American support of Diệm in refusing elections was seen as thwarting the democracy that the United States claimed to support. Kennedy, while senator, opposed involvement. Many young people protested because they were being drafted, others because the anti-war movement grew popular among the counterculture. Some within the peace movement advocated unilateral withdrawal. Opposition to the war tended to unite groups opposed to US anti-communism and imperialism, and for those involved with the New Left. Others, such as Stephen Spiro, opposed the war based on the theory of Just War. Some wanted to show solidarity with the Vietnamese, such as Norman Morrison emulating Thích Quảng Đức.

The draft mobilized substantial protest among young people, helping the antiwar movement gain traction within the broader counterculture of the era. Within the peace movement, some advocates argued for unilateral U.S. withdrawal, while others united against what they viewed as American anti-communism and imperialism, bringing together groups such as the New Left. Individual proponents offered varied ethical foundations, including Stephen Spiro’s invocation of Just War theory to oppose the conflict. In addition, certain activists sought solidarity with the Vietnamese people, with Norman Morrison notably emulating Thích Quảng Đức in an act intended to highlight the war’s human costs.

Peirce take truth to have some manner of essential relation to human practices for inquiring into and discovering truth, with Peirce himself holding that truth is what human inquiry would find out on a matter, if our practice of inquiry were taken as far as it could profitably go: "The opinion which is fated to be ultimately agreed to by all who investigate, is what we mean by the truth ..."
ai_text: Truth is closely tied to human practices of inquiry and the pursuit of knowledge. For the American philosopher Charles Sanders Peirce, truth is the eventual outcome of inquiry—that is, the proposition that would be disclosed if inquiry were carried as far as it can profitably go. The core claim of this view is that truth is the opinion destined to be universally accepted by all investigators in the long run.

human_text: Logic is concerned with the patterns in reason that can help tell if a proposition is true or not. Logicians use formal languages to express the truths they are concerned with, and as such there is only truth under some interpretation or truth within some logical system.
ai_text: Truth, within the study of logic, concerns whether a given proposition correctly corresponds to the reasoning it expresses. Logicians analyze patterns in reasoning to determine the validity or truth of statements by examining the relationships between premises and conclusions and the broader implications of arguments. To facilitate precise analysis, they employ formal languages and symbolic frameworks that allow truths to be articulated and evaluated with rigor. In this view, truth is not absolute in a vacuum but is defined relative to an interpretation of the language or to the axioms and inference rules that govern a particular logical system.

human_text: Tatai Wildlife Sanctuary (Khmer: ដែនជម្រកសត្វព្រៃតាតៃ) is a protected area in southwest Cambodia created in 2016, covering 144,275 ha (356,510 acres). Located in the Cardamom Mountains, the area is threatened by sand dredging and processing, by the filling-in of water bodies, and by land-grabbing. In 2021, 26,103 ha (64,500 acres) were cut from the wildlife sanctuary in a PADDD event. Local communities have been displaced into the protected area from nearby areas following the creation of the 246-megawatt Stung Tatai hydropower dam by China National Machinery Industry Corporation in 2014.

Compared with Layer II, Layer I imposes lower computational complexity, facilitating real-time encoding on hardware available circa 1990.

The Strait of Gibraltar serves as the gateway to the Mediterranean Sea, which is considered a marginal sea of the Atlantic. human_text: For centuries, Chinese opera was the main form of entertainment for both urban and rural residents in China as well as the Chinese diaspora. Its popularity declined sharply in the second half of the 20th century as a result of both political and market factors. Language policies discouraging topolects in Taiwan and Singapore, official hostility against rural religious festivals in China, and de-Sinicization in Taiwan have all been blamed for the decline of various forms in different times, but overall the two major culprits were Cultural Revolution — which saw traditional culture systematically erased, innumerable theatre professionals viciously persecuted, and younger generation raised with far lesser exposure to Chinese opera – and modernization, with its immense social impact and imported values that Chinese opera has largely failed to counter. The total number of regional genres was determined to be more than 350 in 1957, but in the 21st century the Chinese government could only identify 162 forms for its intangible cultural heritage list, with many of them in immediate danger of disappearing. For young people, Chinese opera is no longer part of the everyday popular music culture, but it remains an attraction for many older people who find in it, among other things, a national or regional identity.

During the Cultural Revolution, traditional cultural forms were eradicated, many theatre professionals were persecuted, and exposure to opera among the younger generation diminished. In the modernization era, sweeping social changes and imported values weakened opera’s appeal, and it largely failed to counter these trends. Regional genres numbered more than 350 in 1957, and by the 21st century the government identified 162 forms for the intangible cultural heritage list, with many regarded as endangered. For younger audiences, Chinese opera is no longer part of everyday popular music culture, though it retains appeal for many older people who associate it with national or regional identity.

The characters in Canjun Opera are thought to be the forerunners of the fixed role categories of later Chinese opera, particularly of its comic chou (丑) characters.

human_text: Radio stations usually report the power of their transmitters in units of watts, referring to the effective radiated power. This refers to the power that a half-wave dipole antenna would need to radiate to match the intensity of the transmitter's main lobe.
ai_text: In radio broadcasting, transmitter power is commonly reported as effective radiated power (ERP), expressed in watts. ERP is defined as the amount of power a hypothetical half-wave dipole antenna would need to radiate to produce the same peak radiation intensity in the main lobe as the actual antenna system. Consequently, ERP provides a link between the transmitter’s output and the resulting radiation level in the main lobe, offering a standardized means of characterizing radiated power.

A glassblower shapes the initial form, after which the piece is repeatedly dipped into molten glass to accumulate several successive layers of color. The layered material is then carved to produce a textured image, with the contrasting colors of the different strata revealed as the outer layers are removed. Historically, many examples employ yellow glass, referred to as Imperial Yellow, reflecting its association with the Qing dynasty’s Aisin Gioro clan.

human_text: Peking glass originated in 18th century China during the rule of the Qing dynasty. While China had long been a major producer of glassware, the introduction of European technologies to Asia in the 17th century caused a shift in the styles of Chinese glass makers. The principle couriers of these technologies were Jesuit missionaries, who introduced modern glass-making methods from Italy to China, which was at the time closed to the West. The advances spurred by the Jesuits led the Kangxi Emperor to establish an Imperial glass-works in 1696 to better produce the new material. The glass was commonly used in snuff bottles and vases, where it was used to imitate the harder to work jade and other precious stones. Eventually, the process of creating Peking glass was spread outside of the imperial glass-works and into the general population, leading to many artisans adopting Peking glass as a medium. The golden age of Peking glass in China is widely cited as being the reign of the Qianlong Emperor in the mid-18th century. Though the art-form declined after the 19th century, the production of Peking glass continued in China through the Republican period and into the present day.

One view is that the system has worked relatively well in the last 30 years, and has tended to shift the federal courts' caseload to the desired balance. Other legal observers have criticized the increasing powers of magistrate judges, who are neither appointed by the President nor confirmed by the Senate. On the other hand, the selection of a magistrate judge is a merit-based process which, by statute, requires public notice of a vacancy and the appointment of a merit selection panel which includes both lawyers and at least two non-lawyers. The panel is required to consider the attributes of each candidate, including scholarship, experience, knowledge of the court system, and personal attributes such as intelligence, honesty and morality, maturity, demeanor, temperament, and ability to work with others. Applicants for the post must be personally interviewed and recommended for the position. In 1878, the Ganz factory, Budapest, Hungary, began manufacturing equipment for electric lighting and, by 1883, had installed over fifty systems in Austria-Hungary. human_text: The Liber Usualis (Liber Usualis missæ et officii pro Dominicis et festis cum cantu Gregoriano or "Book for Use at Masses and Offices of Sundays and Feasts with their Gregorian Chants") is a liturgical book of commonly used Gregorian chants in the Catholic tradition, compiled by the monks of the Abbey of Solesmes in France and first published in 1898. It gathered between two covers the ordinary and proper chants from the Kyriale and Graduale needed for Masses of Sunday and important Holy Days; those for Vespers from the Antiphonale; and Matins of Christmas, Holy Week and the Office of the Dead from the Nocturnale. Its most important omissions are the chants for the weekdays of Lent and the Ember Days.
ai_text: Liber Usualis is a liturgical compendium of Gregorian chants widely used in the Catholic tradition. It was compiled by the monks of the Abbey of Solesmes in France and first published in 1898. The volume consolidates ordinary and proper chants from the Kyriale and Graduale for Sundays and major holy days, and it also incorporates the Vespers chants from the Antiphonale. Furthermore, it includes Matins chants for Christmas, Holy Week, and the Office of the Dead drawn from the Nocturnale. Notable omissions include the chants assigned to the weekdays of Lent and Ember Days. The work’s Latin designation refers to a Book for Use at Masses and Offices of Sundays and Feasts with Gregorian chants, and it is commonly known in English as Book for Use at Masses and Offices of Sundays and Feasts with their Gregorian Chants.

human_text: The Liber was first edited in 1896 by Solesmes Abbot Dom André Mocquereau (1849–1930). Its use has decreased since the liturgical reform that took place in 1970, that replaced the Tridentine Mass with the Mass of Paul VI, and the Divine Office with the Liturgy of the Hours. In 1974 a new Graduale Romanum (and in 1990 a Gregorian Missal) appeared in response to the same council's mandate that Gregorian chant should retain "pride of place" in the liturgy (Sacrosanctum Concilium, 116). It resigned the traditional chants according to the new calendar, but introduction of the vernacular has hindered widespread use of Latin chant. The 1964 Liber usualis continues to be used locally where permission exists for celebrations according to the vetus ordo.
ai_text: The Liber Usualis, a comprehensive compilation of Gregorian chant used in the Latin liturgy, was first edited in 1896 under the direction of Solesmes Abbot Dom André Mocquereau (1849–1930). Its prominence declined after the 1970 liturgical reforms, which replaced the Tridentine Mass with the Mass of Paul VI and the Divine Office with the Liturgy of the Hours. In response to Vatican II’s mandate that Gregorian chant be accorded a principal role in liturgy (Sacrosanctum Concilium, 116), the 1974 Graduale Romanum and the 1990 Gregorian Missal were issued. The revision aligned the chant practice with the new liturgical calendar, discontinuing much of the traditional repertory, and the spread of the vernacular languages limited the widespread use of Latin chant. The 1964 Liber Usualis continues to be used locally where permission exists for celebrations according to the vetus ordo.

ai_text: Prediction Units (PUs) in the Audio Video Standard define all prediction modes available to Coding Units (CUs) and serve as the fundamental unit for both intra-frame and inter-frame prediction. A PU’s size is constrained by the size of the CU to which it belongs and cannot exceed it. In AVS1, intra-frame prediction is enhanced by introducing non-square block partitions in addition to the conventional square partitions. For inter-frame prediction, the framework adopts a symmetric partitioning scheme but adds four asymmetric partition modes, broadening the range of allowable partition configurations.

ai_text: Microfiltration is a membrane-based separation process that uses relatively large pores. In contrast, nanofiltration membranes provide pores in the range of 0.001–0.01 μm and are capable of separating multivalent ions, synthetic dyes, sugars, and certain salts while permitting smaller molecules to pass. The transition from microfiltration to nanofiltration, with decreasing pore size, is associated with a higher requirement for osmotic pressure to sustain filtration.

human_text: Aside from the above applications, MF membranes have found dynamic use in major areas within the dairy industry, particularly for milk and whey processing. However, the most promising technique for MF membranes in this field pertains to the separation of casein from whey proteins (i.e. serum milk proteins).  This results in two product streams both of which are highly relied on by consumers; a casein-rich concentrate stream used for cheese making, and a whey/serum protein stream which is further processed (using ultrafiltration) to make whey protein concentrate. The whey protein stream undergoes further filtration to remove fat in order to achieve higher protein content in the final WPC (Whey Protein Concentrate) and WPI (Whey Protein Isolate) powders.
ai_text: Microfiltration (MF) membranes are used in dairy processing to treat milk and whey, enabling the selective rejection of bacteria and spores and thereby enhancing product safety. As a pre-treatment step, MF can precede pasteurisation and contribute to extended shelf-life. The most notable application of MF is the separation of casein from whey (serum) proteins, producing two streams: a casein-rich concentrate for cheese production and a whey-derived serum protein stream for further processing. The whey stream is then subjected to ultrafiltration to yield whey protein concentrate (WPC), and subsequent fat removal by additional filtration raises the protein content to support the production of WPC products and whey protein isolate (WPI) powders.

In comparative terms, notable counterparts include the United States' Electronic System for Travel Authorization (ESTA) and the United Kingdom's Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA).

human_text: The European banking union refers to the transfer of responsibility for banking policy from the member state-level to the union-wide level in several EU member states, initiated in 2012 as a response to the 2009 Eurozone crisis. The motivation for the banking union was the fragility of numerous banks in the Eurozone, and the identification of a vicious circle between credit conditions for these banks and the sovereign credit of their respective home countries ("bank-sovereign vicious circle"). In several countries, private debts arising from a property bubble were transferred to the respective sovereign as a result of banking system bailouts and government responses to slowing economies post-bubble. Conversely, weakness in sovereign credit resulted in deterioration of the balance sheet position of the banking sector, not least because of high domestic sovereign exposures of the banks.
ai_text: The European banking union is a framework that transfers banking policy responsibility from national authorities to a union-wide level in several EU member states. It was launched in 2012 in response to the 2009 Eurozone crisis, with the aim of addressing the fragility of many Eurozone banks and the bank–sovereign vicious circle that links bank credit conditions to sovereign credit strength. In some countries, private debts arising from a property bubble were effectively shifted to the sovereign through bailouts and subsequent government actions after the bubble burst. Compounding these pressures, weak sovereign credit also worsened banks’ balance sheets due to high domestic sovereign exposures.

ai_text: The Apuan Alps originate from marine sediments deposited during the middle Triassic, predating the rest of the Apennines and exhibiting a distinct geological configuration. Over time those sediments consolidated into rock types including limestone, dolomite, sandstone, and shale. Around 25 million years ago, substantial tectonic pressure transformed much of the limestone into the celebrated Carrara marble. The marble derives its name from the nearby city of Carrara. The range is widely associated with Carrara marble as a defining feature. Erosion subsequently sculpted the remaining sedimentary rocks into a rugged karst landscape.

human_text: Some cases can be disposed of without the need for a trial. In fact, the vast majority are. This reduced sentence is sometimes a reward for sparing the state the expense of a formal trial. ai_text: The vast majority of criminal cases are resolved without a trial through non-trial dispositions. When the accused admits guilt, the process is typically shorter and sentencing can occur more quickly. Plea bargaining exists in some jurisdictions—most notably in the United States—and may involve negotiated pleas of guilty, no contest, or not guilty; such arrangements can include diversionary measures or reduced penalties, especially when the prosecution’s case is weak or in exchange for cooperation. Reduced sentences achieved through plea bargains can also lower the costs associated with conducting a formal trial. By contrast, many countries do not permit plea bargaining, arguing that it can coerce innocent defendants into pleading guilty to avoid harsher punishment. At the same time, courts are increasingly seeking alternatives to incarceration, favoring measures that divert offenders from immediate imprisonment where appropriate.

This characterization of vipassanā’s focus has been attributed to the scholar Damien Keown.

ai_text: The Noble Eightfold Path is a principal framework in Buddhism that comprises eight interrelated factors designed to promote ethical conduct, mental discipline, and wisdom. When developed together, these factors lead to the cessation of dukkha, the Buddhist term for unsatisfactory experience or suffering. The eight elements are Right View (or Understanding), Right Intention (or Thought), Right Speech, Right Action, Right Livelihood, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, and Right Concentration.

human_text: Maximilian's death came at a time when Dürer was concerned he was losing "my sight and freedom of hand" (perhaps caused by arthritis) and increasingly affected by the writings of Martin Luther. In July 1520 Dürer made his fourth and last major journey, to renew the Imperial pension Maximilian had given him and to secure the patronage of the new emperor, Charles V, who was to be crowned at Aachen. Dürer journeyed with his wife and her maid via the Rhine to Cologne and then to Antwerp, where he was well received and produced numerous drawings in silverpoint, chalk and charcoal. In addition to attending the coronation, he visited Cologne (where he admired the painting of Stefan Lochner), Nijmegen, 's-Hertogenbosch, Bruges (where he saw Michelangelo's Madonna of Bruges), Ghent (where he saw Jan van Eyck's Ghent Altarpiece), and Zeeland.

human_text: Because Dürer left autobiographical writings and was widely known by his mid-twenties, his life is well documented. After a few years of school, Dürer learned the basics of goldsmithing and drawing from his father. Though his father wanted him to continue his training as a goldsmith, he showed such a precocious talent in drawing that he was allowed to start as an apprentice to Michael Wolgemut at the age of fifteen in 1486. A self-portrait, a drawing in silverpoint, is dated 1484 (Albertina, Vienna) "when I was a child", as his later inscription says. The drawing is one of the earliest surviving children's drawings of any kind, and, as Dürer's Opus One, has helped define his oeuvre as deriving from, and always linked to, himself. Wolgemut was the leading artist in Nuremberg at the time, with a large workshop producing a variety of works of art, in particular woodcuts for books. Nuremberg was then an important and prosperous city, a centre for publishing and many luxury trades. It had strong links with Italy, especially Venice, a relatively short distance across the Alps.

page_title: International Standard Identifier for Libraries and Related Organizations
human_text: An ISIL consists of a prefix identifying the authority which issued the ISIL, a dash, and then an identifier issued by that authority. All two letter prefixes are reserved for the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, followed by an identifier assigned by that country's national library authority. Global-level identifiers can also be assigned, which are not associated with a particular country, e.g. 'oclc-' for the OCLC. The suffix is generally a pre-existing system of identifying libraries; thus, ISIL unifies existing systems around the world rather than instituting an entire system from scratch.
ai_text: An ISIL consists of a prefix identifying the issuing authority, a hyphen, and then an identifier issued by that authority. Two-letter prefixes are reserved for ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes, and after the country code the national library authority assigns the specific identifier. There are also global-level identifiers not linked to any country, for example the oclc- prefix used by the Online Computer Library Center. The suffix relies on an existing system for identifying libraries rather than creating a new scheme. Overall, ISIL serves to unify pre-existing library identification systems worldwide rather than establishing an entirely new framework.
