human_text: Laser scanning describes the general method to sample or scan a surface using laser technology. Several areas of application exist that mainly differ in the power of the lasers that are used, and in the results of the scanning process. Low laser power is used when the scanned surface doesn't have to be influenced, e.g. when it only has to be digitised. Confocal or 3D laser scanning are methods to get information about the scanned surface. Another low-power application uses structured light projection systems for solar cell flatness metrology, enabling stress calculation throughout in excess of 2000 wafers per hour.
ai_text: 3D scanning encompasses techniques for capturing the shape of physical objects, with laser scanning serving as a method to sample surfaces by projecting and detecting laser light. The range of applications depends on the laser power and the nature of the resulting data, and lower power is often employed when it is important not to influence the surface being scanned, such as during digitisation. Confocal methods and other three-dimensional laser scanning approaches are used to derive quantitative information about surface geometry. In low‑power contexts, structured light projection systems are applied for solar cell flatness measurements, enabling rapid assessment and, consequently, stress calculations for large production runs, with more than 2,000 wafers processed per hour.

human_text: Silhouette techniques use outlines created from a sequence of photographs around a three-dimensional object against a well contrasted background. These silhouettes are extruded and intersected to form the visual hull approximation of the object. With these approaches some concavities of an object (like the interior of a bowl) cannot be detected.
ai_text: Silhouette-based 3D scanning relies on outlines extracted from a sequence of photographs taken around an object against a high-contrast background. The resulting silhouettes are extruded into volumetric prisms along the corresponding viewing directions, and the intersections of these volumes yield the visual hull, an approximate representation of the object's outer shape. A notable limitation of this approach is its inability to capture certain concavities, such as the interior of a bowl, because hidden geometry cannot be recovered from silhouette information alone.

human_text: Democracy is Freedom – The Daisy (Italian: Democrazia è Libertà – La Margherita, DL), commonly known simply as The Daisy (La Margherita), was a centrist political party in Italy. The party was formed from the merger of three parties within the centre-left coalition: the Italian People's Party, The Democrats and Italian Renewal. The party president and leader was Francesco Rutelli, former mayor of Rome and prime ministerial candidate during the 2001 general election for The Olive Tree coalition, within which The Daisy electoral list won 14.5% of the national vote.
ai_text: Democrazia è Libertà – La Margherita (DL), commonly known as The Daisy (La Margherita), was a centrist political party in Italy that emerged from the merger of three centre-left groups—the Italian People's Party, The Democrats, and Italian Renewal—within the broader centre-left coalition. It was led by Francesco Rutelli, a former mayor of Rome, who served as party president and stood as its prime ministerial candidate in the 2001 general election as part of the Olive Tree coalition. In that election, The Daisy's list secured about 14.5 percent of the national vote.

human_text: The idea of uniting the centrist components of The Olive Tree, which were divided in many parties, was discussed at least from 1996. In the 1996 general election, there were actually two centrist lists within the Italian centre-left coalition: the Populars for Prodi, an electoral list including the Italian People's Party (PPI), Democratic Union (UD), the Italian Republican Party (PRI) and the South Tyrolean People's Party (SVP), and that of Italian Renewal (RI), including the Segni Pact (PS) and Italian Socialists (SI), which later merged into the Italian Democratic Socialists (SDI) in 1998. In 1998 splinters from the centre-right coalition formed the Democratic Union for the Republic (UDR), later transformed into Union of Democrats for Europe (UDEUR), to support the D'Alema I Cabinet. In 1999 splinters of PPI, UD and other groups formed The Democrats (Dem), while the Union for the Republic (UpR), a breakaway group from the UDR, the SDI and the PRI joined forces in The Clover, a short-lived alliance.

human_text: From the first United States Census in 1790 to the 1960 Census, the government's census enumerators chose a person's race. Racial categories changed over time, with different groups being added and removed with each census. Since the 1970 Census, Americans provide their own racial self-identification. This change was due to the reforms brought about by the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965, which required more accurate census data. Since the 1980 Census, in addition to their race or races, all respondents are categorized by membership in one of two ethnic categories, which are "Hispanic or Latino" and "Not Hispanic or Latino." This practice of separating "race" and "ethnicity" as different categories has been criticized both by the American Anthropological Association and members of US Commission on Civil Rights.
ai_text: The treatment of Native American identities in the U.S. Census has shifted markedly from the late 18th century to the present, reflecting broader changes in the government’s approach to race and ethnicity. From 1790 through 1960, census takers determined an individual's race, with racial categories evolving across successive decennial censuses. Beginning with the 1970 census, individuals began to self-identify their race, a change driven by reforms associated with the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965 aimed at producing more accurate population data. Since the 1980 census, the survey has separately classified respondents by both race and ethnicity, explicitly distinguishing Hispanic or Latino from Not Hispanic or Latino. This methodological separation has attracted criticism from bodies such as the American Anthropological Association and the U.S. Commission on Civil Rights, which have questioned the validity and utility of bifurcating race and ethnicity in census data.

human_text: The London equations, developed by brothers Fritz and Heinz London in 1935, are constitutive relations for a superconductor relating its superconducting current to electromagnetic fields in and around it. Whereas Ohm's law is the simplest constitutive relation for an ordinary conductor, the London equations are the simplest meaningful description of superconducting phenomena, and form the genesis of almost any modern introductory text on the subject. A major triumph of the equations is their ability to explain the Meissner effect, wherein a material exponentially expels all internal magnetic fields as it crosses the superconducting threshold.
ai_text: Developed by Fritz and Heinz London in 1935, the London equations are a set of constitutive relations that relate the superconducting current to the electromagnetic fields inside and around a superconductor. They provide the most straightforward description of superconducting phenomena, in contrast to Ohm's law for ordinary conductors. The framework formed the genesis of virtually all modern introductory treatments of superconductivity. In particular, the equations account for the Meissner effect, describing the exponential expulsion of magnetic fields from the interior of a material as it transitions into the superconducting state.

human_text: PRINT supported comma and semicolon separating parameters, the former moving the cursor to the next 16-character wide column, the later leaving the cursor at the end of the printed value. It supported the TAB() function, but not SPC(). In common with other "high end" BASICs of the era, Wang BASIC offered formatted output with PRINTUSING and a separate "image". The image was defined using a separate line starting with the percent sign, for instance, 180 % ##,###.## and then using that format with 190 PRINTUSING 180, N. Any characters other than the formatting characters were echoed back during the print, so one could define a complete output with something like 180 % ANGLE= #.#### RADIANS.
ai_text: Wang BASIC provides refined control over output through its PRINT statement, which accepts both comma and semicolon as parameter separators: the comma advances the cursor to the next 16-character-wide column, while the semicolon leaves the cursor at the end of the printed value. TAB() is supported as a formatting function, whereas SPC() is not implemented. In addition, the language offers formatted output via a dedicated PRINTUSING facility paired with a separate image that defines the formatting rules. An image is defined on a line that begins with a percent sign, such as a line like 180 % ##,###.##, and it can be invoked with 190 PRINTUSING 180, N to render the value N in that specified format. Characters that are not part of the image’s formatting codes are echoed during printing, enabling fully customized output that can include fixed text around the numeric value, for example text like ANGLE= and RADIANS surrounding the formatted number.

human_text: Missing features that were addressed in 2200B included the addition of ON...GOTO and ON...GOSUB. KEYIN read a character from the keyboard without pausing, similar to INKEY$ in MS BASIC. VAL searched a string and returned a numeric value within it. The NUM function was similar to LEN, but returned the length of the substring up to the first non-numeric character. For instance, if A$ is "1234.5", NUM(A$) would return 6, whereas if A$ was "1234.5    ", NUM would return 10, because spaces are valid in numbers.
ai_text: Wang BASIC, a dialect of the BASIC programming language used on Wang systems, received notable enhancements with the 2200B revision, including the addition of the ON...GOTO and ON...GOSUB multi-branching constructs that had been absent previously. The KEYIN command enables reading a single character from the keyboard without requiring a pause, and is comparable to MS BASIC's INKEY$ routine. The VAL function is designed to search a string and extract the numeric value embedded within it. The NUM function, while akin to LEN in purpose, returns the length of the numeric substring from the start of a string up to the first non-numeric character, with spaces considered valid within numbers; for example NUM("1234.5") = 6 and NUM("1234.5    ") = 10.

human_text: A town is a classification of municipalities used in British Columbia. British Columbia's lieutenant governor may incorporate a community as a town by letters patent, under the recommendation of the Minister of Communities, Sport and Cultural Development, if its population is greater than 2,500 but not greater than 5,000 and the outcome of a vote involving affected residents was that greater than 50 percent voted in favour of the proposed incorporation.
ai_text: Within British Columbia, the designation of town constitutes a particular class of municipalities. A community may pursue incorporation as a town by means of letters patent, a process that requires the endorsement of the provincial Minister of Communities, Sport and Cultural Development. The incorporation pathway is limited to communities whose population falls between 2,501 and 5,000 residents. In addition, the proposal must be approved by those affected through a referendum, with more than half of the voters casting a yes vote for incorporation to be realized.

human_text: Mamberamo was born from the confluence of two large inland rivers. Tariku comes from the west to the east and Taritatu from the east. These rivers meander through swamps with huge internal descents and then merge. The Mamberamo thus formed reaches the ocean by breaking through the Coastal Mountains. Mamberamo River is navigable to Marine Falls. The Sepik is a much more important river. Similarly, it collects water from a spacious pool. It is 1,100 kilometers from the Victor Emanuel Range to the estuary, making it the longest river in New Guinea. The winding, muddy, sluggish river can be navigated for 500 km. Ramu is a 650 km long river. Its lower section is navigable, but its upper flow is high-falling, fast-flowing. The energy of the river is used by a power plant near the city of Kainantu.
ai_text: The Mamberamo River in New Guinea is formed where the Tariku, which runs from west to east, joins the Taritatu, coming from the east; the river then threads swampy terrain with substantial internal descents before its confluence, and it reaches the ocean after breaking through the Coastal Mountains, remaining navigable up to Marine Falls. The Sepik River is the island’s more important watercourse, gathering waters from a broad pool and extending roughly 1,100 kilometers from the Victor Emanuel Range to its estuary, making it the longest river in New Guinea; its course is winding, its waters muddy and sluggish, and navigation is feasible for about 500 kilometers. The Ramu River runs roughly 650 kilometers, with the lower section suitable for navigation while the upper reaches exhibit a high-gradient, fast-flowing regime, and its energy is utilized by a hydroelectric plant near Kainantu.

human_text: With some 786,000 km2 of tropical land—less than one-half of one percent (0.5%) of the Earth's surface—New Guinea has an immense biodiversity, containing between 5 and 10 percent of the total species on the planet. This percentage is about the same amount as that found in the United States or Australia. A high percentage of New Guinea's species are endemic, and thousands are still unknown to science: probably well over 200,000 species of insect, between 11,000 and 20,000 plant species, and over 650 resident bird species. Most of these species are shared, at least in their origin, with the continent of Australia, which was until fairly recent geological times part of the same landmass (see Australia-New Guinea for an overview). The island is so large that it is considered 'nearly a continent' in terms of its biological distinctiveness.

The region supports a remarkable share of global biodiversity, with estimates placing roughly five to ten percent of all living species on the planet within its borders, a proportion comparable to that found in the United States or Australia. A large portion of its flora and fauna are endemic, and thousands of species remain unknown to science. Current estimates identify more than 200,000 insect species, between 11,000 and 20,000 plant species, and over 650 resident bird species. Most of its taxa trace their origins to lineages shared with Australia, reflecting their common paleogeographic history, as Australia and New Guinea were part of the same landmass until relatively recent geological times. Given its vast size and distinctive ecological assemblages, the island is often regarded as nearly a continent in terms of biological distinctiveness.

human_text: The politicians who had risen to power during the 1830s had by then become familiar with the difficulties and pitfalls of power. According to historian Roderick J. Barman, by 1840, "they had lost all faith in their ability to rule the country on their own. They accepted Pedro II as an authority figure whose presence was indispensable for the country's survival." Some of these politicians (who would form the Conservative Party in the 1840s) believed that a neutral figure was required—one who could stand above political factions and petty interests to address discontent and moderate disputes. They envisioned an emperor who was more dependent on the legislature than the constitutional monarch envisioned by Pedro I, yet with greater powers than had been advocated at the beginning of the Regency by their rivals (who later formed the Liberal Party). The liberals, however, contrived to pass an initiative to lower Pedro II's age of majority from eighteen to fourteen. The Emperor was declared fit to rule in July 1840.

ai_text: Teleophthalmology employs telecommunications technologies to enable remote assessment and management of eye health. Central to its practice is fundus photography, in which retinal images are captured with a fundus camera. A fundus camera is a specialized, low-magnification microscope that integrates an attached camera, purpose-built to obtain detailed views of the retina for evaluation by clinicians who may be distant from the patient.

human_text: Mobile applications are widely available in ophthalmology and optometry as tools for eye tests (visual acuity, colour test, and viewing eye images) and for educational purposes. Technological advancements in digital ocular imaging devices are perceived by many as key drivers for teleophthalmology. Recently, emerging retinal imaging modalities such as optical coherence tomography are capable of producing digital images of the retina with a micrometer resolution, which can be transmitted for research or diagnostic purposes. Along with systems designed for health care professionals, patient-centred systems such as Eye-File Archived 2022-03-14 at the Wayback Machine for use by the general public are emerging.

human_text: As the number of Spanish settlers grew in Alta California, the boundaries and natural resources of the mission properties became disputed. Conflicts between the Crown and the Church arose over land. State and ecclesiastical bureaucrats debated over authority of the missions. The Franciscan priests of Mission Santa Clara de Asís sent a petition to the governor in 1782 which stated that the Mission Indians owned both the land and cattle and represented the Ohlone against the Spanish settlers in nearby San José. The priests reported that Indians' crops were being damaged by the pueblo settlers' livestock and that the settlers' livestock was also "getting mixed up with the livestock belonging to the Indians from the mission" causing losses. They advocated that the Indigenous people be allowed to own property and have the right to defend it.

human_text: Richard Garner, arguably among the first dedicated primate field researchers, personified this tendency. He recorded primate vocalizations and tested the animal's responses when played back. But his writings included anthropomorphized claims about monkey and ape "speech," stories that provided fodder for outlandish newspaper headlines and illustrations.

ai_text: El (Cyrillic) refers to the Cyrillic letter Л, used across several Slavic languages. In most Slavic languages employing the Cyrillic script, a distinct orthographic convention exists to indicate whether the lateral /l/ is hard or soft. Consequently, the letter Л can represent either a hard [l] or a softened [l], with the actual pronunciation determined by the following letter in the spelling. This particular distinction is not applied in the same way in Serbian and Macedonian.

human_text: Almost all known substances undergo thermal expansion in response to heating, meaning that a given mass of substance contracts to a low volume at low temperatures, when little thermal energy is present.  Substances, especially fluids in which intermolecular forces are weak, also undergo compression upon the application of pressure.  Nearly all substances therefore reach a density maximum at very low temperatures and very high pressures, characteristic properties of the solid state of matter.
ai_text: Maximum density refers to the phenomenon by which a substance attains its greatest density under conditions of very low temperature and, in some cases, high pressure. In general, most materials expand when heated, leading to a increase in volume with rising temperature; conversely, at sufficiently low temperatures a given mass occupies a smaller volume, resulting in a higher density. Moreover, many substances—especially weakly interacting fluids—are compressible and shrink in volume when pressure is applied. Taken together, these tendencies imply that nearly all substances exhibit a density maximum at extreme low temperatures and elevated pressures. This density maximum is regarded as a characteristic property of the solid state of matter.

human_text: An especially notable irregular maximum density is that of water, which reaches a density peak at 4 °C (39 °F). This has important ramifications in Earth's ecosystem.
ai_text: Water exhibits an anomalous density behavior in which its density increases as temperature falls until it reaches a maximum at about 4 °C (39 °F); below this temperature, further cooling causes density to decrease as water nears the freezing point. This unusual density peak has important ramifications for Earth's ecosystems, influencing the vertical structure and mixing of aquatic systems, shaping the distribution of nutrients and dissolved oxygen, and thereby affecting habitat conditions for aquatic organisms, particularly in temperate regions where seasonal stratification and turnover are tied to this property.

The batsman is declared out if he remains outside the crease when the bails are dislodged.

ai_text: In the study of Hindu units of time, verse 1.71 has been interpreted in different ways by traditional commentators and modern scholars. Bühler’s translation, which is also endorsed by Jones, renders 1.71 as twelve thousand years within a four-aged period, a reading grounded in Kulluka Bhatta’s commentary. By contrast, Medhatithi interprets the verse as twelve thousand four-aged periods within an age of the gods. This interpretation is rejected by Kulluka Bhatta and by Olivelle, who argue that 1.79 mentions twelve thousand without a qualifier such as etat (this), thereby indicating that the measurement should be read as years rather than as four-aged periods.

human_text: The history of humanity is divided up into four yugas (a.k.a. dharmic ages or world ages)—Kṛta-yuga (pronounced Krita-yuga; a.k.a. Satya-yuga), Tretā-yuga, Dvāpara-yuga and Kali-yuga—each with a 25% decline in dharmic practices and length, giving proportions (caraṇas; pronounced charanas) of 4:3:2:1 (e.g. Satya: 100% start; Kali: 25% start, 0% end), indicating a de-evolution in spiritual consciousness and an evolution in material consciousness. Kali-yuga is followed by Satya-yuga of the next cycle, where a cycle is called a catur-yuga (pronounced chatur-yuga; a.k.a. mahā-yuga). Each yuga is divided into a main period (a.k.a. yuga proper) and two yuga-sandhis (a.k.a. yuga-sandhyās; connecting periods)⁠—yuga-sandhyā (dawn) and yuga-sandhyāṃśa (a.k.a. yuga-sandhyānśa; dusk)⁠—where each yuga-sandhi lasts for 10% of the main period. Lengths are given in divine years (a.k.a. celestial or Deva years), where a divine year lasts for 360 solar (human) years. A chatur-yuga lasts for 4.32 million solar (12,000 divine) years with 1,728,000 years of Krita-yuga, 1,296,000 years of Treta-yuga, 864,000 years of Dvapara-yuga, and 432,000 years of Kali-yuga.
ai_text: Hindu cosmology presents time as a catur-yuga, or mahā-yuga, a fourfold cycle comprising Krita (Satya) yuga, Treta yuga, Dvāpara-yuga, and Kali yuga. Across a catur-yuga, the dharmic practices and the lengths of the successive yugas diminish by a quarter, producing a 4:3:2:1 ratio with Satya yuga being the most virtuous and Kali yuga the least; in moral terms, Satya begins at full strength and Kali ends at zero. After Kali yuga, the cycle recommences with Satya yuga in the next iteration, making a complete catur-yuga the mahā-yuga. Each yuga is divided into a main period and two yuga-sandhis (dawn and dusk), with each sandhi lasting 10% of the main period. The durations are measured in divine years, where one divine year equals 360 solar years; consequently a catur-yuga totals 12,000 divine years, or about 4.32 million solar years, with Krita-yuga lasting 1,728,000 solar years, Treta-yuga 1,296,000, Dvāpara-yuga 864,000, and Kali-yuga 432,000.

human_text: Following the Vue Mai incident, debate over the Hmong's planned repatriation to Laos intensified, including in the United States, where it drew opposition from American conservatives and some human rights advocates. In 1996 as the deadline for the closure of Thai refugee camps approached, and under mounting political pressure, the United States agreed to resettle Hmong refugees who passed a screening process. Around 5,000 Hmong people who were not resettled at the time of the camp closures sought asylum at Wat Tham Krabok, a Buddhist monastery in central Thailand where more than 10,000 Hmong refugees had already been living. The Thai government attempted to repatriate these refugees, and the Wat Tham Krabok Hmong refused to leave and the Lao government refused to accept them, claiming they were involved in the illegal drug trade and were of non-Lao origin. Following threats of forcible removal by the Thai government, the United States, in a victory for the Hmong, agreed to accept 15,000 of the refugees in 2003. Several thousand Hmong people, fearing forced repatriation to Laos if they were not accepted for resettlement in the United States, fled the camp to live elsewhere within Thailand where a sizeable Hmong population has been present since the 19th century.

Around ten percent belong to other lowland communities; together with the Lao, these groups constitute the Lao Loum, or lowland people.

human_text: Within philosophy of science, this view is often an answer to the question "how is the success of science to be explained?" The discussion on the success of science in this context centers primarily on the status of unobservable entities apparently talked about by scientific theories. Generally, those who are scientific realists assert that one can make valid claims about unobservables (viz., that they have the same ontological status) as observables, as opposed to instrumentalism.
ai_text: Scientific realism is a view in the philosophy of science that seeks to explain the notable success of scientific theories by maintaining that they track not only observable phenomena but also unobservable aspects of the world. The central issue concerns the ontological status of entities that are not directly accessible to sense perception but are posited by scientific theories. Realists argue that statements about such unobservables can be true or approximately true and that these unobservables hold a status similar to that of observable entities. This position contrasts with instrumentalism, which treats theories as merely predictive tools for observable outcomes without committing to the real existence of unobserved entities.

human_text: Holmium-chromium-thulium triple-doped yttrium aluminium garnet (Ho:Cr:Tm:YAG, or Ho,Cr,Tm:YAG) is an active laser medium material with high efficiency. It lases at 2080 nm in the infrared and is widely used in military applications, medicine, and meteorology. Single-element thulium-doped YAG (Tm:YAG) lasers operate at 2010 nm. The wavelength of thulium-based lasers is very efficient for superficial ablation of tissue, with minimal coagulation depth in air or in water. This makes thulium lasers attractive for laser-based surgery.
ai_text: Thulium is utilized in solid-state laser systems, notably in configurations that combine holmium, chromium, and thulium doping within a yttrium aluminum garnet host. The Ho:Cr:Tm:YAG arrangement, a triple-doped crystal, serves as a highly efficient active laser medium and emits light at approximately 2080 nanometers in the infrared. By contrast, lasers based on a single-element Tm:YAG medium produce radiation near 2010 nanometers. The thulium-based emission wavelengths are especially well suited to superficial tissue ablation with shallow coagulation depths, both in air and in water, which makes these lasers attractive for laser-assisted surgery. In addition to medical applications, thulium lasers find use in meteorology for atmospheric sensing and in military contexts. Together, these attributes underlie the appeal of thulium-based laser systems for precise, minimally invasive procedures and reliable infrared laser sources.

human_text: In World War I, the British Blue Book was the second collection of national diplomatic documents about the war to appear; it came out just days after the German White Book. It contained 159 items and was submitted to Parliament before the session of 6 August 1914, after the British declaration of war on Germany. It appeared later in an expanded, and somewhat different version, and included an introduction and reports from parliamentary sessions in the beginning of August under the title, Great Britain and the European Crisis. This version contained the same 159 items from the first one, plus two more from the British embassies in Vienna and Berlin, after the outbreak of the war. Although incomplete (e.g., files on the English promises of aid to France, and on German concessions and proposals are not included), it is the richest of the color books and, in the view of Max Beer, "despite its gaps, constitutes a true treasure trove of historical insights into the great crisis".

The various frequency components propagate as sound waves that overlap and sum through the air, a phenomenon described by the principle of superposition. The relative amplitudes, or balance, of these constituent frequencies largely determine the instrument's characteristic timbre.

human_text: In simple terms, timbre is what makes a particular musical instrument or human voice have a different sound from another, even when they play or sing the same note. For instance, it is the difference in sound between a guitar and a piano playing the same note at the same volume. human_text: A block is performed when, after a shot is attempted, a defender succeeds in altering the shot by touching the ball. In almost all variants of play, it is illegal to touch the ball after it is in the downward path of its arc; this is known as goaltending. It is also illegal under NBA and Men's NCAA basketball to block a shot after it has touched the backboard, or when any part of the ball is directly above the rim. Under international rules it is illegal to block a shot that is in the downward path of its arc or one that has touched the backboard until the ball has hit the rim. After the ball hits the rim, it is again legal to touch it even though it is no longer considered as a block performed.
ai_text: In basketball, a block occurs when a defender touches the ball in flight after a shooter releases a shot and alters its trajectory. Goaltending refers to contacting the ball during its downward arc toward the rim, which is illegal. Under NBA and men's NCAA rules, it is prohibited to block a shot once the ball has touched the backboard or while any part of the ball is directly above the rim. By contrast, international rules forbid blocking the ball in the downward arc or after it has touched the backboard until the ball hits the rim. Once the ball makes contact with the rim, touching it becomes legal again, though such contact is no longer considered a block.

human_text: A tradition is a system of beliefs or behaviors (folk custom) passed down within a group of people or society with symbolic meaning or special significance with origins in the past. A component of cultural expressions and folklore, common examples include holidays or impractical but socially meaningful clothes (like lawyers' wigs or military officers' spurs), but the idea has also been applied to social norms and behaviors such as greetings, etc. Traditions can persist and evolve for thousands of years— the word tradition itself derives from the Latin  word tradere literally meaning to transmit, to hand over, to give for safekeeping. While it is reportedly assumed that traditions have an ancient history, many traditions have been invented on purpose, whether it be political or cultural, over short periods of time. Various academic disciplines also use the word in a variety of ways.

The concept also extends to customary social norms and greetings. Traditions can endure for millennia, persisting and evolving in response to changing circumstances. human_text: The phrase "according to tradition" or "by tradition" usually means that what follows is known only through oral tradition and is not supported (and might even be refuted) by solid evidence. Here, "tradition" describes the source or nature of the information. For example, "According to tradition, Homer was born on Chios, but many other places have historically claimed him as theirs." This tradition may never be proven or disproved. Another example is, "King Arthur, according to history, a true British king, has inspired many well loved stories." Whether the claims are supported by evidence or not does not reduce their value as cultural history and literature.
ai_text: Tradition denotes information transmitted through oral cultural practices rather than independent documentary evidence, and as such may lack solid verification or be susceptible to challenge. The phrase according to tradition or by tradition signals that the claim derives from customary retellings rather than established records, thereby indicating its traditional source rather than being corroborated. An illustrative case is the attribution of Homer’s birthplace to Chios by tradition, a claim that many places contest and which may never be definitively proven or disproven. Similarly, statements such as “King Arthur, according to history, a true British king,” have nonetheless spurred extensive storytelling. Regardless of their evidentiary status, traditional claims retain value as components of cultural history and literature, offering insight into collective memory and the ways communities imagine their past.

human_text: Baptism transforms the old and sinful person into a new and pure one; the old life, the sins, any mistakes made are gone and a clean slate is given. Through Baptism a person is united to the Body of Christ by becoming a member of the Orthodox Church. During the service, water is blessed. The catechumen is fully immersed in the water three times, once in the name of each of the figures of the Holy Trinity. This is considered to be a death of the "old man" by participation in the crucifixion and burial of Christ, and a rebirth into new life in Christ by participation in his resurrection. Properly a new name is given, which becomes the person's name.

A distinctive feature of the service is the blessing of the water, which is employed in the baptismal act. The catechumen is fully immersed in the water three times, each immersion performed in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. This immersion signifies the death of the old self with Christ’s crucifixion and burial, followed by rebirth through his resurrection. In many cases, a new name is conferred at baptism, and this name becomes the individual’s baptismal name.

human_text: In June 1836, the French newspaper La Presse was the first to include paid advertising in its pages, allowing it to lower its price, extend its readership and increase its profitability and the formula was soon copied by all titles. Around 1840, Volney B. Palmer established the roots of the modern day advertising agency in Philadelphia. In 1842 Palmer bought large amounts of space in various newspapers at a discounted rate then resold the space at higher rates to advertisers. The actual ad – the copy, layout, and artwork – was still prepared by the company wishing to advertise; in effect, Palmer was a space broker. The situation changed when the first full-service advertising agency of N.W. Ayer & Son was founded in 1869 in Philadelphia. Ayer & Son offered to plan, create, and execute complete advertising campaigns for its customers. By 1900 the advertising agency had become the focal point of creative planning, and advertising was firmly established as a profession.

In 1856, the Florida department was established. On 7 July 1880, Río Negro was split from Paysandú and Rocha from Maldonado. In 1884, Treinta y Tres was formed from parts of Cerro Largo and Minas, Artigas was detached from Salto, and Rivera was detached from Tacuarembó. By contrast, happiness presupposes an evaluative stance toward a span of life or one’s life as a whole, signifying a judgment about overall well-being rather than an immediate affect tied to the ongoing pursuit.

human_text: Human-centered computing researchers and practitioners usually come from one or more disciplines such as computer science, human factors, sociology, psychology, cognitive science, anthropology, communication studies, graphic design, and industrial design. Some researchers focus on understanding humans, both as individuals and in social groups, by focusing on the ways that human beings adopt and organize their lives around computational technologies. Others focus on designing and developing new computational artifacts.
ai_text: Human-centered computing is an interdisciplinary field that integrates computer science with disciplines such as human factors, sociology, psychology, cognitive science, anthropology, communication studies, graphic design, and industrial design. It covers research into how individuals and social groups adopt, adapt to, and organize their lives around computational technologies, as well as efforts to design and develop new computational artifacts that support human activities. By combining studies of use with the creation of technological tools, the field seeks to understand the social and cognitive dimensions of computing and to produce systems and interfaces that align with human needs and practices.

human_text: Based on the principles of human-centered computing, the Center for Cognitive Ubiquitous Computing (CUbiC) at Arizona State University develops assistive, rehabilitative and healthcare applications. Founded by Sethuraman Panchanathan in 2001, CUbiC research spans three main areas of multimedia computing: sensing and processing, recognition and learning, and interaction and delivery. CUbiC places an emphasis on transdisciplinary research and positions individuals at the center of technology design and development. Examples of such technologies include the Note-Taker, a device designed to aid students with low vision to follow classroom instruction and take notes, and VibroGlove, which conveys facial expressions via haptic feedback to people with visual impairments.

human_text: In computing, endianness is the order in which bytes within a word data type are transmitted over a data communication medium or addressed in computer memory, counting only byte significance compared to earliness. Endianness is primarily expressed as big-endian (BE) or little-endian (LE).
ai_text: Endianness denotes the arrangement of bytes within a word, and it has implications for both data transmission over communication channels and the addressing of bytes in computer memory. It determines the significance order of the bytes, indicating which byte carries the most significant value. In common usage, endianness is described using two principal schemes: big-endian, where the most significant byte is placed or transmitted first, and little-endian, where the least significant byte is placed or transmitted first.

human_text: Both types of endianness are in widespread use in digital electronic engineering. The initial choice of endianness of a new design is often arbitrary, but later technology revisions and updates perpetuate the existing endianness to maintain backward compatibility. Big-endianness is the dominant ordering in networking protocols, such as in the Internet protocol suite, where it is referred to as network order, transmitting the most significant byte first. Conversely, little-endianness is the dominant ordering for processor architectures (x86, most ARM implementations, base RISC-V implementations) and their associated memory. File formats can use either ordering; some formats use a mixture of both or contain an indicator of which ordering is used throughout the file.

In networking, big-endian is the standard convention, referred to as network order, with the most significant byte transmitted first. By contrast, little-endian predominates in processor architectures and memory layouts, as illustrated by x86, the majority of ARM implementations, and the base RISC-V design. File formats, meanwhile, may adopt either ordering; some formats combine both and others explicitly indicate the ordering in use.

ai_text: Amid the early phase of the French Revolution, a vigorous British political debate arose over the legitimacy of popular sovereignty and reform. Central to this discourse were two influential pamphlets that articulated support for Richard Price and the notion that the French people possessed the right to overhaul their state. Mary Wollstonecraft's A Vindication of the Rights of Men is among the earliest of these pamphlets, arguing for political reform and the universality of rights. A few months later, Thomas Paine's Rights of Man expanded on the same line of thought, challenging hereditary privilege and defending the revolution's principles. In 1792, Christopher Wyvill published Defence of Dr. Price and the Reformers of England, advocating gradual, moderate reform within constitutional bounds. Collectively, these works are described as a defining strand of British political debate during the era and are regarded as one of the great exchanges in British political history.

human_text: The frame rate of 1080i is usually 50 or 60 Hz. It depends on the region. In areas using the PAL or SECAM standards, like Europe and parts of Asia, the frame rate is 50 Hz. In regions using NTSC, like North America and Japan, the frame rate is 60 Hz. The frame rate refers to how often a new field is shown per second. At 50 Hz, 50 fields are shown each second. This results in 25 full frames per second when the odd and even fields are combined. At 60 Hz, 59.94 fields are shown per second. This results in 29.97 full frames per second. Interlacing affects how motion is perceived in 1080i. Since each field represents a slightly different moment in time, motion can appear smoother compared to lower frame rate progressive scans. However, this also means 1080i can struggle with fast-moving scenes. The interlaced fields might not perfectly align, leading to motion artifacts. The European Broadcasting Union (EBU) prefers to use the resolution and frame rate (not field rate) separated by a slash, as in 1080i/29.97 and 1080i/25, likewise 480i/29.97 and 576i/25. Resolutions of 1080i59.94 or 1080i50 often refers to 1080i/29.97 or 1080i/25 in EBU notation.
ai_text: 1080i is an HD interlaced video format that uses two fields per frame to produce the full picture, with the field rate depending on the broadcasting region: 50 Hz in PAL/SECAM areas and 60 Hz in NTSC areas, corresponding to 50 fields per second or 59.94 fields per second, respectively. When the two fields are paired, 50 Hz yields 25 full frames per second, while 59.94 Hz yields 29.97 full frames per second. Interlacing alternates between fields captured at slightly different moments in time, which can smooth motion compared with progressive scanning at similar effective frame rates, but it may also generate motion artifacts in fast-moving scenes if the field alignment is imperfect. The EBU notation prefers the resolution and frame rate to be presented in a slash-separated format, with examples such as 1080i/29.97 and 1080i/25 (paralleling 480i/29.97 and 576i/25). In EBU terms, 1080i59.94 is understood as 1080i/29.97, and 1080i50 corresponds to 1080i/25.

The match was contested by Sporting CP and CSKA Moscow on 18 May 2005;  CSKA won the match 3–1. Sporting CP opened the scoring in the first half from full-back Rogério, before Aleksei Berezutskiy equalised in the second half. Yuri Zhirkov would give the Russian side the lead nine minutes after CSKA's equalising goal, and the Moscow outfit would close out the scoring 15 minutes from the end after a quick CSKA counterattack saw Vágner Love become the youngest player to score in a UEFA Cup final at the age of 20 years, 341 days, firing the ball past Sporting goalkeeper Ricardo to give the Russian side a first UEFA Cup trophy. These developments have made it feasible to run the algorithm on embedded devices, including mobile phones, broadening its practical applications.

human_text: Code-excited linear prediction (CELP) is a linear predictive speech coding algorithm originally proposed by Manfred R. Schroeder and Bishnu S. Atal in 1985. At the time, it provided significantly better quality than existing low bit-rate algorithms, such as residual-excited linear prediction (RELP) and linear predictive coding (LPC) vocoders (e.g., FS-1015). Along with its variants, such as algebraic CELP, relaxed CELP, low-delay CELP and vector sum excited linear prediction, it is currently the most widely used speech coding algorithm. It is also used in MPEG-4 Audio speech coding. CELP is commonly used as a generic term for a class of algorithms and not for a particular codec.

Over the years, multiple variants have been developed, including algebraic CELP, relaxed CELP, low-delay CELP, and vector sum excited linear prediction (VSELP). Today, CELP and its variants are among the most widely used speech coding methods, and CELP-based techniques are employed in MPEG-4 Audio speech coding. It is important to note that CELP is a generic term for a class of algorithms rather than a single codec.

human_text: In music theory, the recapitulation is one of the sections of a movement written in sonata form.  The recapitulation occurs after the movement's development section, and typically presents once more the musical themes from the movement's exposition.  This material is most often recapitulated in the tonic key of the movement, in such a way that it reaffirms that key as the movement's home key.

human_text: In some sonata form movements, the recapitulation presents a straightforward image of the movement's exposition. human_text: The first historical mention of the Pharisees and their beliefs comes in the four gospels and the Acts of the Apostles, in which both their meticulous adherence to their interpretation of the Torah as well as their eschatological views are described. A later historical mention of the Pharisees comes from the Jewish-Roman historian Josephus in a description of the "four schools of thought", or "four sects", into which he divides the Jews in the 1st century AD. (The other schools were the Essenes, who were generally apolitical, and may have emerged as a sect of dissident priests who rejected either the Seleucid-appointed or the Hasmonean high priests as illegitimate; the Sadducees, who were the main antagonists of the Pharisees; and the Zealots.) Other sects may have emerged at this time, such as the early Christians in Jerusalem and the Therapeutae in Egypt. However, their status as Jews is unclear.

The Essenes are described as generally apolitical and possibly dissident priests opposing certain high-priestly factions. By contrast, the Sadducees are often portrayed as the principal opponents of the Pharisaic movement, while the Zealots represent another distinct faction. In addition to these groups, early Christian communities in Jerusalem and the Therapeutae in Egypt are contemporary currents, though the precise status of these groups within Judaism remains a matter of scholarly debate.

The Pharisees believed that all Jews in their ordinary life, and not just the Temple priesthood or Jews visiting the Temple, should observe rules and rituals concerning purification.

For the Pharisees, ordinary Jewish life should be permeated by rules and rituals concerning purification, not solely by Temple-centered practice.

human_text: Harlingerland Frisian is an extinct dialect of the East Frisian language. It was known for giving several features originally in Old Frisian. The language was only documented in the year 1691 with the book Memoriale linguae Frisicae, by Johann Cadovius-Müller. This dialect then slowly vanished and was displaced by the Harlings dialect of Low German. It belonged to the Weser dialects alongside the Wursten and Wangerooge Frisian dialects.

Over time the dialect faded away as it was displaced by the Harlings dialect of Low German. In classification, Harlingerland Frisian belonged to the Weser group of East Frisian dialects, alongside the Wursten and Wangerooge Frisian varieties.

ai_text: Dei Seoi Naamyam constitutes a distinctive Cantonese regional form of narrative song performance that rose to prominence in the 20th century amid the flourishing teahouse culture of Canton, Hong Kong, and Macao. Its presentations were commonly held in teahouses as well as on streets and in brothels, and the tradition was traditionally performed by blind singers known as the blind master (瞽師). Notable pieces in the repertoire include the piece commonly rendered as Hegemon-King Bids His Lady Farewell (霸王别姬) along with Nan Siu Yi (男燒衣) and Nui Siu Yi (女燒衣). The art form entered a decline in the late 1920s as Cantonese opera gained popularity, and it was subsequently adapted into Cantonese Opera, where it became known as Hei Kuk Naamyam.

ai_text: Highest median voting rules encompass Bucklin's rule and its reversal, often called Anti-Bucklin. ai_text: Highest median voting rules are electoral procedures in which voters provide evaluative scores for candidates rather than producing a full rank-order. The winner is the candidate whose median evaluation, calculated across all ballots, is the highest. Because these rules rely on cardinal judgments and use the median as the summary statistic, they circumvent Arrow's impossibility theorem, which applies to certain ordinal aggregation schemes. They satisfy the unanimity criterion and the independence of irrelevant alternatives, ensuring that unanimous support for a candidate yields that candidate's victory and that the outcome depends only on the evaluations of the candidates under consideration. However, they fail to satisfy the near-unanimity criterion, meaning that a scenario with broad but not universal agreement may not guarantee the chosen candidate aligns with that near-consensus.

Projections indicate that ongoing global warming could drive further rises in sea level in the future. Even modest increases could threaten many coastal cities through increased flooding and inundation of low-lying zones. Additionally, rising seas influence coastal landforms, drowning and reshaping glacially carved valleys, which contributes to the formation or enlargement of features such as fjords and rias.

human_text: In lectures and throughout the body of his work, Vico's rhetoric begins from a central argument (medius terminus), which is to be clarified by following the order of things as they arise in our experience. Probability and circumstance retain their proportionate importance, and discovery—reliant upon topics (loci)—supersedes axioms derived through reflective, abstract thought. In the tradition of classical Roman rhetoric, Vico sets out to educate the orator (rhetorician) as the transmitter of the oratio, a speech with ratio (reason) at the centre. What is essential to the oratorical art (Gr. ῥητορική, rhētorikē) is the orderly link between common sense and an end commensurate with oratory; an end that is not imposed upon the imagination from above (in the manner of the moderns and dogmatic Christianity), but that is drawn from common sense, itself.  In the tradition of Socrates and Cicero, Vico's true orator will be midwife to the birth of "the true" (as an idea) from "the certain", the ignorance in the mind of the student.

Since the early 1920s amateur radio operators (or "hams"), limited to lower transmitter power than broadcast stations, have taken advantage of skywave for long-distance (or "DX") communication.

The majority of long-distance shortwave communication, in the band roughly 3 to 30 MHz, depends on skywave effects. Since the early 1920s, amateur radio operators, commonly called hams, have exploited skywave with relatively low transmitter power to achieve long-distance DX communication.

human_text: In contemporary Orthodox Judaism there is dispute as to the status of the Zohar's and Isaac Luria's (the Arizal) Kabbalistic teachings. While a portion of Modern Orthodox, followers of the Dor De'ah movement, and many students of the Rambam reject Arizal's Kabbalistic teachings, as well as deny that the Zohar is authoritative or from Shimon bar Yohai, all three of these groups accept the existence and validity of the Talmudic Maaseh Breishit and Maaseh Merkavah mysticism. Their disagreement concerns whether the Kabbalistic teachings promulgated today are accurate representations of those esoteric teachings to which the Talmud refers. The mainstream Haredi (Hasidic, Lithuanian, Oriental) and Religious Zionist Jewish movements revere Luria and the Kabbalah, but one can find both rabbis who sympathize with such a view, while disagreeing with it, as well as rabbis who consider such a view heresy. The Haredi Eliyahu Dessler and Gedaliah Nadel maintained that it is acceptable to believe that the Zohar was not written by Shimon bar Yochai and that it had a late authorship. Yechiel Yaakov Weinberg mentioned the possibility of Christian influence in the Kabbalah with the "Kabbalistic vision of the Messiah as the redeemer of all mankind" being "the Jewish counterpart to Christ."
ai_text: In contemporary Orthodox Judaism, the status of the Zohar and Isaac Luria’s Kabbalistic teachings remains a topic of ongoing debate. Certain Modern Orthodox groups centered on Dor De’ah and a large share of Rambam study circles reject the Arizal’s Kabbalah and deny the Zohar’s authority or its attribution to Shimon bar Yochai, although they may accept, in principle, elements of mystical tradition such as Ma’aseh Bereshit and Ma’aseh Merkavah. The central dispute concerns whether present-day Kabbalistic teachings faithfully reflect the esoteric contents referenced in Talmudic literature. By contrast, mainstream Haredi and Religious Zionist currents generally revere Luria and the Kabbalah, yet rabbinic opinions vary widely, with some leaders sympathetic, others critical, and some orthodox voices deeming such reverence inappropriate or even heretical. Among Haredi authorities, figures like Eliyahu Dessler and Gedaliah Nadel maintained that it is permissible to doubt Shimon bar Yochai’s authorship of the Zohar and to regard its composition as late. Additionally, Yechiel Yaakov Weinberg has suggested possible Christian influence on Kabbalah, pointing to a messianic vision of universal redemption as a Jewish parallel to Christian conceptions of Christ.

ai_text: Research into Moken children's underwater vision has led scientists to rule out several alternative explanations for their performance, and they concluded that the Moken did not evolve enhanced underwater sight through a trade-off that would transfer focusing power from the cornea to the lens; moreover, the Moken’s eyes are not nearsighted, and their ability to adjust lens power is not superior to that of other groups. In parallel work, Gislén and colleagues trained European children to see better underwater by crossing their eyes, a practice that increases lens power and reduces pupil diameter. After the training, the European children were able to see underwater as well as the Moken children, suggesting that comparable underwater acuity can be achieved through specific ocular adjustments rather than population-specific adaptations.

ai_text: Ria Cheyne contends that representations of disability are widely regarded as inherently regressive. These depictions tend to reduce individuals to their impairment rather than recognizing their full humanity and social identities. The so-called supercrip trope has drawn sustained critique for implying that disability should be associated with extraordinary talent, genius, or insight. Such framing engenders unrealistic expectations about what people with disabilities should be capable of, and underscores the need for more nuanced, person-centered portrayals that reflect everyday experiences and capabilities.

human_text: The political/relational model is an alternative to and critical engagement with both the social and medical models. This analytic posed by Alison Kafer shows not only how the "problem" of disability "is located in inaccessible buildings, discriminatory attitudes, and ideological systems that attribute normalcy and deviance to particular minds and bodies" but also how mind and bodily impairments can still have disabling effects. Furthermore, the political/relational model frames the medicalization of disabled folks as political in nature given it should always be interrogated.
ai_text: Within disability studies, the political/relational model offers an alternative to both the social and medical frameworks by foregrounding how political structures, institutions, and interpersonal relationships shape disability. Alison Kafer argues that the central problem lies in inaccessible environments, discriminatory attitudes, and ideologies that normalize some minds and bodies while stigmatizing others. She also contends that impairments of mind or body can continue to produce disabling experiences through barriers and exclusion, even when the individual is not medicated by a medical account. In this view, the medicalization of disability is a political question that warrants critical examination and challenge, rather than a straightforward explanation of disability.

human_text: Probable and probability, along with their cognates in other modern languages, derive from medieval learned Latin probabilis. This term, first used by Cicero, was  generally applied to opinions to mean plausible or generally approved. The form probability entered through Old French probabilite in the fourteenth century, borrowed directly from the Latin probabilitatem, itself derived from probabilitas and carrying the sense of credibility or likelihood. Thus probabilitas sits at the root of the lineage, stemming from probabilis. The modern, mathematical sense of probability as a quantitative measure of chance emerged later, with the term taking on its formal meaning in 1718.

human_text: Taking advantage of internal conflicts which emerged in the Holy Roman Empire after Emperor Otto II's death, Géza invaded Bavaria and took the fortress of Melk in 983. Furthermore, he renounced the lands east of the river Leitha in his peace treaty of 996 with Henry IV of Bavaria. Géza also arranged the marriage of his son and heir Stephen to Henry IV's sister Giselle. Even before this marriage alliance, Géza convoked the Hungarian leaders to an assembly and forced them to take an oath confirming his son's right to succeed him.

human_text: Géza succeeded his father around 972. He adopted a centralizing policy, which gave rise to his fame as a merciless ruler. The longer version of his son's Life even states that Géza's hands were "defiled with blood". Pál Engel wrote that Géza carried out a "large-scale purge" against his relatives, which explains the lack of references to other members of the Árpád dynasty from around 972. Koppány, who continued to rule the southern parts of Transdanubia, is the only exception to this dearth of references. A marriage alliance between the German and Byzantine dynasties brought about a rapprochement between the two powers neighboring Hungary in 972. Géza decided to make peace with the Holy Roman Empire. human_text: Data structures serve as the basis for abstract data types (ADT). The ADT defines the logical form of the data type. The data structure implements the physical form of the data type.
ai_text: Data structures are the concrete means by which data is stored and organized in computer memory. They provide the foundation on which abstract data types (ADTs) are built, since ADTs encapsulate the intended operations and logical behavior of a data type. Conversely, ADTs specify the conceptual form of a data type, while data structures realize that form by supplying a concrete physical representation and layout that enables the practical implementation of the associated operations.

human_text: Data structures provide a means to manage large amounts of data efficiently for uses such as large databases and internet indexing services. Usually, efficient data structures are key to designing efficient algorithms. Some formal design methods and programming languages emphasize data structures, rather than algorithms, as the key organizing factor in software design. Data structures can be used to organize the storage and retrieval of data stored in both main memory and secondary memory.

The effectiveness of algorithms often depends on the underlying data structures, as their organization can significantly influence performance and scalability. In some formal design methodologies and programming languages, data structures are treated as the primary organizing principle of software design, at times taking precedence over algorithmic considerations. Data structures govern how data is stored and retrieved across both main memory and secondary storage, shaping access patterns and efficiency in practice.

This emphasis on harmonic succession supported Baroque basso continuo practice, in which bass lines were sustained while chords implied above provided the harmonic framework. The shift demanded a more vertical approach to composition and elevated the triad to the fundamental building block of functional harmony.

human_text: Induction AC motors may be used as generators, turning mechanical energy into electric current. Induction generators operate by mechanically turning their rotor faster than the simultaneous speed, giving negative slip. A regular AC non-simultaneous motor usually can be used as a generator, without any changes to its parts. Induction generators are useful in applications like minihydro power plants, wind turbines, or in reducing high-pressure gas streams to lower pressure, because they can recover energy with relatively simple controls. They do not require another circuit to start working because the turning magnetic field is provided by induction from the one they have. They also do not require speed governor equipment as they inherently operate at the connected grid frequency.
ai_text: Induction AC motors can function as generators, converting mechanical energy into electrical energy when the rotor speed exceeds the synchronous speed, a condition known as negative slip. They do not require a separate starting circuit because the rotating magnetic field is produced by the driven source. Likewise, they do not require speed governor equipment, since their operation is inherently synchronized to the connected grid frequency.

human_text: Condorraptor and Piatnitzkysaurus are generally grouped together within this family in a clade excluding Marshosaurus. Due to the strong resemblance to Piatnitzkysaurus, it has been suggested that Condorraptor could be better interpreted as the result of individual variation within the species and not a separate taxon. human_text: Northern Asia was glaciated in the Pleistocene, but this played a less significant part in the geology of the area compared to the part that it played in North America and Europe. The Scandinavian ice sheet extended to the east of the Urals, covering the northern two thirds of the Ob Basin and extending onto the Angara Shield between the Yenisei River and the Lena River. There are legacies of mountain glaciation to be found on the east Siberian mountains, on the mountains of the Kamchatka Peninsula, on the Altai, on Tian Shan, and on other small areas of mountains, ice caps remain on the islands of Severnaya Zemlya and Novaya Zemlya, and several Central Asian mountains still have individual glaciers. North Asia itself has permafrost, ranging in depths from 30 to 600 metres and covering an area of 9.6 million km2.

A lasting legacy of mountain glaciation is evident in the eastern Siberian ranges, the Kamchatka Peninsula, the Altai, and the Tian Shan, with contemporary ice caps persisting on Severnaya Zemlya and Novaya Zemlya and glaciers remaining on several Central Asian peaks. human_text: Deep technical diving usually involves the use of several breathing gas mixtures during the course of the dive. There will be a mixture known as the bottom gas, which is optimised for limiting inert gas narcosis and oxygen toxicity during the deep sector of the dive. This is generally the mixture which is needed in the largest amount for open circuit diving, as the consumption rate will be greatest at maximum depth. The oxygen fraction of the bottom gas suitable for a dive deeper than about 65 metres (213 ft) will not have sufficient oxygen to reliably support consciousness at the surface, so a travel gas must be carried to start the dive and get down to the depth at which the bottom gas is appropriate. There is generally a large overlap of depths where either gas can be used, and the choice of the point at which the switch will be made depends on considerations of cumulative toxicity, narcosis and gas consumption logistics specific to the planned dive profile.
ai_text: Deep technical diving often relies on the use of more than one breathing gas during a single dive. The bottom gas is formulated to minimize both inert gas narcosis and oxygen toxicity in the deep portion of the ascent, while in open-circuit configurations it usually represents the largest portion of gas carried due to higher consumption at depth. For dives extending beyond approximately 65 metres (213 feet), the bottom gas’s oxygen fraction would not reliably sustain consciousness if breathed at surface pressures, which prompts the use of a travel gas carried from the surface to begin the dive and reach the intended depth. There remains a substantial overlap in the depths at which either gas can be employed, depending on the planned profile. The decision as to where to switch from one gas to the other is made by considering cumulative toxicity, narcosis risk, and the practicalities of gas budgeting for the overall dive plan.

human_text: A delayed stop occurs when the ascent rate is slower than the nominal rate for a table. A computer will automatically allow for any theoretical ingassing of slow tissues and reduced rate of outgassing for fast tissues, but when following a table, the table will specify how the schedule should be adjusted to compensate for delays during the ascent. Typically a delay in reaching the first stop is added to bottom time, as ingassing of some tissues is assumed, and delays between scheduled stops are ignored, as it is assumed that no further ingassing has occurred. This may be considered a special case of a multi-level dive.
ai_text: Decompression practice encompasses methods used to manage ascent in order to minimize decompression stress. A delayed stop occurs when the ascent rate is slower than the table’s nominal rate, causing the planned decompression stops to be encountered later than expected. Computers used for decompression modeling account for the theoretical ingassing of slow tissues and the reduced outgassing of fast tissues, thereby refining the schedule. When using a table, the ascent schedule should be adjusted to compensate for these delays, including adding a delay to the bottom time before reaching the first decompression stop to reflect assumed ingassing. Delays between scheduled stops are generally ignored, under the assumption that no further ingassing has occurred during those intervals. In this sense, decompression practice can be regarded as a specific instance of a multi-level dive framework.

human_text: One of the most pronounced features of early Renaissance European art music was the increasing reliance on the interval of the third and its inversion, the sixth. (In the Middle Ages, thirds and sixths had been considered dissonances; and consonances were derived only of the perfect intervals: the perfect fourth, the perfect fifth, the octave, and the unison). Polyphony—the use of multiple, independent melodic lines played simultaneously—became increasingly elaborate throughout the 14th century, with highly independent voices in both vocal music and instrumental music. The beginning of the 15th century showed simplification, with the composers often striving for smoothness in the melodic parts. This was possible because of a greatly increased vocal range in music. Previously, in the Middle Ages, the narrow vocal range necessitated frequent crossing of parts, thus requiring a greater contrast between them to distinguish the different parts.
ai_text: In the early Renaissance, composers increasingly treated the interval of a third and its inversion, the sixth, as a foundation for harmony, marking a shift from medieval practice in which thirds and sixths were regarded as dissonant and consonance was defined primarily by perfect intervals such as the octave, unison, fourth, and fifth. The 14th century saw polyphony become more intricate, with voices—whether sung or played on instruments—developing greater independence. At the beginning of the 15th century, musical texture began to simplify and favor smoother melodic lines. This smoothing was made possible by a substantially expanded vocal range, which reduced the need for voice crossing and allowed clearer, more continuous melodic contours across parts.

human_text: Ogham (also ogam and ogom,  OG-əm, Modern Irish: [ˈoː(ə)mˠ]; Middle Irish: ogum, ogom, later ogam [ˈɔɣəmˠ]) is an Early Medieval alphabet used primarily to write the early Irish language (in the "orthodox" inscriptions, 4th to 6th centuries AD), and later the Old Irish language (scholastic ogham, 6th to 9th centuries). There are roughly 400 surviving orthodox inscriptions on stone monuments throughout Ireland and western Britain, the bulk of which are in southern areas of the Irish province of Munster. The Munster counties of Cork and Kerry contain 60% of all Irish ogham stones. The largest number outside Ireland are in Pembrokeshire, Wales.

In traditional inscriptions it is dated to the 4th through the 6th centuries CE, with later use for Old Irish (scholastic ogham) extending from the 6th to the 9th centuries. Approximately 400 orthodox inscriptions survive on stone monuments across Ireland and western Britain. The majority of these inscriptions come from Munster in southern Ireland, particularly the counties of Cork and Kerry, which together contain about 60 percent of all Irish ogham stones. The largest concentration outside Ireland is found in Pembrokeshire, Wales. Ogham is also known as ogam and ogom.

human_text: It is generally thought that the earliest inscriptions in Ogham date to about the 4th century AD, but James Carney believed its origin is rather within the 1st century BC. Although the use of classical ogham in stone inscriptions seems to have flourished in the 5th and 6th centuries around the Irish Sea, from the phonological evidence it is clear that the alphabet predates the 5th century. Indeed, the alphabet has letters representing archaic phonemes which were clearly part of the system, but which were no longer spoken by the 5th century and never appear in inscriptions, suggesting an extended period of ogham writing on wood or other perishable material prior to the preserved monumental inscriptions. They are: úath ("H") and straif ("Z" in the manuscript tradition, but probably "F" from "SW"), and gétal (velar nasal "NG" in the manuscript tradition, but etymologically probably "GW").

human_text: Pharaoh was a title of the monarch of ancient Egypt used from the Eighteenth Dynasty onwards. The title was subsequently added to all the previous kings of Egypt. Before this Pharaoh was a term that meant more of the kings' administration. The earliest confirmed instance of the title used contemporaneously for a ruler is a letter to Akhenaten (reigned c. 1353–1336 BCE), possibly preceded by an inscription referring to Thutmose III (c. 1479–1425 BCE). Although the title only came into use in the Eighteenth Dynasty during the New Kingdom, scholars today use it for all the rulers of Egypt from the First Dynasty (c. 3150 BCE) until the annexation of Egypt by the Roman Republic in 30 BCE.

Part of the inflow originates from the 154-square-mile Castaic Creek watershed upstream of the dam. The lake is bisected by the Elderberry Forebay Dam, which creates the adjacent Elderberry Forebay. Aqueduct water reaching the lake is conveyed from Pyramid Lake through the Angeles Tunnel. The water drives the Castaic Power Plant, a pumped-storage hydroelectric facility at the northern end of the forebay, with most of the water’s energy used to power the turbines rather than to pump water back uphill.

The TLS mode provides strong encryption of all traffic transmitted on the data channel.
ai_text: SPICE, the Simple Protocol for Independent Computing Environments, defines client connections that are composed of multiple data channels. Data channels can be configured to carry data in unencrypted form or under Transport Layer Security, enabling administrators to adjust the balance between security and performance on a per-channel basis. When TLS is enabled, the entirety of the channel’s traffic is protected by strong encryption.

These actions led to the Spanish people revolting against French occupation and outbreak of the Peninsular War, and ended the Franco-Spanish alliance in the Napoleonic Wars.

All of the former Confederate states were represented in Congress for the first time since they seceded from the Union.

human_text: The biggest change in this census was in racial classification. Enumerators were instructed to no longer use the "Mulatto" classification. Instead, they were given special instructions for reporting the race of interracial persons. A person with both white and black ancestry (termed "blood") was to be recorded as "Negro", no matter the fraction of that lineage (the "one-drop rule"). A person of mixed black and American Indian ancestry was also to be recorded as "Neg" (for "Negro") unless they were considered to be "predominantly" American Indian and accepted as such within the community. A person with both white and American Indian ancestry was to be recorded as American Indian, unless their Indigenous ancestry was small, and they were accepted as white within the community. In all situations in which a person had white and some other racial ancestry, they were to be reported as that other race. People who had minority interracial ancestry were to be reported as the race of their father.
ai_text: During a period of reform in the U.S. Census, racial classifications were reorganized to replace the term mulatto and to introduce explicit guidelines for reporting individuals of mixed heritage. A one-drop rule was applied, whereby a person with white and black ancestry was recorded as Negro regardless of the relative proportion of white or black ancestry. For those with mixed black and American Indian lineage, the designation was Negro unless the individual was predominantly American Indian and widely accepted as such within their community. Similarly, individuals with white and American Indian ancestry were classified as American Indian unless Indigenous heritage was minor and they were accepted as white in their community. In cases where a person possessed white ancestry together with any other racial background, the census would assign the race corresponding to that non-white lineage. Additionally, individuals with minority interracial ancestry were recorded as the race of their father.

human_text: The theory of consequences. A consequence is a hypothetical, conditional proposition: two propositions joined by the terms 'if ... then'. For example, 'if a man runs, then God exists' (Si homo currit, Deus est). A fully developed theory of consequences is given in Book III of William of Ockham's work Summa Logicae. There, Ockham distinguishes between 'material' and 'formal' consequences, which are roughly equivalent to the modern material implication and logical implication respectively. Similar accounts are given by Jean Buridan and Albert of Saxony.
ai_text: Within the history of logic, a consequence is defined as a hypothetical conditional proposition of the form “if … then.” A classic illustration is the conditional relation in which an action by a person is linked to the assertion of God’s existence. In his Summa Logicae, Book III, William of Ockham develops a comprehensive account of consequences. Ockham distinguishes between material consequences, corresponding to what is now called material implication, and formal consequences, corresponding to modern deductive (logical) implication. Similar accounts of consequence are found in the works of Jean Buridan and Albert of Saxony.

human_text: The theory of supposition. Supposition theory deals with the way that predicates (e.g., 'man') range over a domain of individuals (e.g., all men). In the proposition 'every man is an animal', does the term 'man' range over or 'supposit for' men existing just in the present, or does the range include past and future men? Can a term supposit for a non-existing individual? Some medievalists have argued that this idea is a precursor of modern first-order logic. "The theory of supposition with the associated theories of copulatio (sign-capacity of adjectival terms), ampliatio (widening of referential domain), and distributio constitute one of the most original achievements of Western medieval logic".
ai_text: Supposition theory is a branch of historical logic that analyzes how predicates and terms extend over a domain of individuals. It examines questions such as in the proposition “every man is an animal” whether the term “man” supposes only present individuals or also those of the past and future, highlighting how reference and predication operate across time. The approach also raises the issue of whether a term can supposit for a non-existing or nonexistent individual, challenging straightforward notions of reference. In medieval scholarship, many thinkers regard this line of inquiry as a precursor to modern first-order logic, anticipating key concerns about quantification and interpretation. Within its broader framework, supposition, together with copulatio (the sign‑capacity of adjectival terms), ampliatio (the widening of the referential domain), and distributio (distribution of terms), is regarded as a major achievement of Western medieval logic, influencing subsequent developments in semantic theory and logical analysis.

The system was further refined by his student Aristophanes of Byzantium, who first introduced the asterisk and used a symbol resembling a ⊤ for an obelus; and finally by Aristophanes' student, in turn, Aristarchus, from whom they earned the name of "Aristarchian symbols".

It originated with Zenodotus, a Homeric scholar, who devised the obelus as part of a broader system of textual-marking symbols. The framework was refined by Aristophanes of Byzantium, who introduced the asterisk and employed a symbol resembling a top (⊤) to signify the obelus, among other marks. Aristophanes’ student Aristarchus expanded the repertoire of these marginal signs, and the collection of symbols associated with him came to be known as the Aristarchian symbols.
